raw.title: Separate orchestration from implementation with a GitHub-native worker exchange
raw.body:
## Capture / admission status

**OWNER-DIRECTED BOUNDED ENABLING SLICE — schedule immediately after #324-R0 and before #318.**

This Work Item records the architecture selected on 2026-09-26 for separating the **orchestrating agent** from the **implementing agent** while keeping GitHub as the first concrete provider/control plane.

It is intentionally smaller than a general multi-agent platform or the optional #15-L4 / #201 executor-fabric work.

Creating this issue does not create a competing branch or PR while #319/VF0 is active. The first bounded slice (**W0**) is owner-admitted for the first safe WIP transition after #324-R0 so that #318 can be the first real semantic dogfood of the separated architecture.

## Problem

Gnostoa has already achieved a useful separation for review:

    implementation candidate
      -> GitHub events / comments
      -> reviewer agents
      -> normalized findings
      -> review convergence

Codex, Claude, Gitar and other reviewers can be invoked through provider-visible triggers rather than through the same chatbot that coordinates the work.

Implementation is still coupled to the orchestrating chatbot. The same long-lived Chat session commonly:

- reconstructs provider/current state;
- decides the next implementation action;
- edits source;
- runs verification;
- publishes a candidate;
- waits for CI/reviews;
- consumes findings;
- repairs the candidate;
- repeats until convergence.

This creates four recurring costs:

1. **session-liveness coupling** — a Chat stall stops both orchestration and implementation;
2. **excess authority** — the orchestrator needs source-write/execution capabilities merely because it also implements;
3. **context amplification** — implementation details, logs and repeated repairs consume the same context needed for semantic coordination;
4. **human recovery toil** — when the session stalls, the owner must Stop/retrigger and wait for stale-state reconciliation.

The desired direction is the same separation already achieved for reviewers:

> **The orchestrator decides what bounded work is required. A replaceable implementation worker authors the proposed change. Deterministic Gnostoa mechanics validate/materialize/publish it. Independent reviewers evaluate the resulting candidate.**

## Desired outcome

Within one admitted Pull Request, ordinary development can proceed autonomously through implementation, verification and review-convergence cycles while:

- the orchestrating agent may be a simple ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini-like chat with minimal provider permissions;
- implementation agents are replaceable workers selected through a generic adapter contract;
- workers do not need merge authority or direct write authority to the canonical PR head;
- GitHub is the first concrete provider-native event/state/dispatch adapter;
- provider/model names do not appear in the generic orchestration contract;
- the owner is needed only for genuine authority/semantic gates, not routine repair loops;
- a stalled/failed worker can be replaced without losing the PR workflow;
- the existing reviewer-agent convergence path composes unchanged.

The common path should approach:

    owner admits scope
      -> orchestrator supplies/approves bounded semantic directive
      -> GitHub/Gnostoa control loop dispatches implementer
      -> worker returns implementation result
      -> deterministic materializer creates exact candidate
      -> CI + reviewer cohort
      -> reducer classifies findings
      -> in-scope repair job automatically dispatched
      -> repeat until convergence
      -> owner merge/authority gate

## Architectural rule

**The Chat session is not the workflow runtime.**

The orchestrating chatbot is a semantic coordinator that may disappear between decisions. Durable workflow state, event reduction, retries, receipts and candidate identities live outside the chat session.

The first concrete control plane is GitHub, but the semantic contract remains provider-neutral.

## Actor separation

The initial responsibility/capability boundary should be mechanically observable, not a prompt convention.

| Actor/component | Repository read | Source authoring | Canonical PR ref write | Review | Merge/authority |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Orchestrating agent | yes | **no** | no | dispatch/reconcile only | no |
| Implementing worker | bounded | sandbox/staging only | **no by default** | no | no |
| Candidate materializer/publisher | deterministic input | apply validated artifact | guarded CAS only | no | no |
| Verification | candidate read/execute | no candidate mutation | no | evidence only | no |
| Reviewer agents | candidate read | no | no | yes | no |
| Accountable owner | as needed | not implied | explicit authority only | disposition where required | protected gate |

This consumes the #10 role/capability model rather than inventing a competing ontology.

## W0 generic abstractions

### 1. ImplementationJob

The orchestrator/controller emits one immutable bounded implementation request.

Illustrative logical shape:

    ImplementationJob
      schema_version
      job_id
      generation
      implementation_id

      subject:
        provider-neutral change subject
        exact base revision/tree
        expected current candidate revision

      objective:
        concise semantic outcome

      scope:
        allowed paths / domains
        explicit non-goals
        allowed change class

      evidence:
        required pre-change mode / receipt
        exact findings or failing behavior to address

      constraints:
        no scope expansion
        forbidden effects
        authority boundaries

      verification:
        focused expectations
        required result evidence

      result_contract:
        accepted result modes

The job is content-addressed. A worker never receives authority merely because it receives a job.

### 2. ImplementationResult

A worker returns a result bound to the exact job/generation:

    ImplementationResult
      schema_version
      job_id
      generation
      exact base observed
      worker/executor provenance
      status

      result:
        PATCH_ARTIFACT | STAGING_REF | DIRECT_PR_HEAD_COMPAT

      changed_paths
      artifact/ref identity
      claimed verification
      limitations / unresolved items
      result digest

The result is **untrusted implementation output**, not a prepared candidate, approval or evidence of correctness.

A result for an old generation is stale even if the patch is otherwise valid.

### 3. AgentDispatchAdapter

The generic controller knows only a small worker contract:

    discover_capabilities()
    dispatch(job)
    observe(attempt)
    collect_result(attempt)
    cancel(attempt)

Capabilities are explicit facts, e.g.:

    machine_triggerable
    can_read_repository
    can_receive_provider_comment
    can_return_patch
    can_write_staging_ref
    can_run_local_tests
    max_context/result constraints

The core does not contain Codex/Claude/Gemini/OmniRoute vocabulary.

### 4. WorkerTransport

Transport is separate from worker semantics.

Initial transport classes:

    GITHUB_COMMENT_TRIGGER
    GITHUB_ACTION_TRIGGER
    API_TRIGGER
    CLI_TRIGGER
    LOCAL_TRIGGER
    MANUAL_RELAY

MANUAL_RELAY is a valid portability fallback, not the semantic baseline for automation.

A simple/free web-chat agent can participate through MANUAL_RELAY without changing the job/result contract. Zero-human implementation requires at least one machine-triggerable worker adapter, but the orchestrating chat itself does **not** need to be machine-triggerable.

### 5. ProviderAdapter

The orchestration core consumes provider-neutral operations such as:

    observe_change()
    collect_events(cursor)
    append_control_event()
    observe_checks()
    observe_reviews()
    update_projection()
    guarded_publish(expected_parent, prepared_result)

The first specialization is GitHubProviderAdapter.

Future GitLab/Forgejo/etc. adapters must not change ImplementationJob/Result semantics.

### 6. CandidateMaterializer

A deterministic/trusted component, not an LLM, converts one accepted worker result into a candidate.

Conceptual path:

    verify job/result identity
      -> verify exact base/current generation
      -> verify result digest
      -> reject forbidden/out-of-scope paths
      -> materialize into isolated exact-parent workspace
      -> enforce VF0 / Decision-0090 preparation
      -> run required focused verification
      -> derive exact prepared tree/receipt
      -> guarded/CAS publication to PR head
      -> record effect receipt

The worker therefore does not need canonical branch credentials.

### 7. ConvergenceReducer

A deterministic reducer consumes current candidate, CI, reviewer and worker state and calculates only legal next effects.

Initial disposition classes:

    ACTIONABLE_IN_SCOPE
    STALE_FINDING
    DUPLICATE_FINDING
    CI_FAILURE_IN_SCOPE
    WAITING_EXTERNAL
    WORKER_FAILED_RETRYABLE
    WORKER_RESULT_STALE
    CONVERGED

    ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED
    OWNER_REQUIRED

Examples:

- fresh in-scope reviewer defect -> automatic ImplementationJob;
- stale/duplicate finding -> no implementation;
- retryable worker failure -> next attempt / compatible worker;
- conflicting semantic findings -> ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED;
- scope expansion / policy ambiguity -> ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED or OWNER_REQUIRED;
- protected merge/readiness gate -> OWNER_REQUIRED.

The reducer cannot turn an agent output into human approval.

## GitHub-native first adapter

GitHub acts as the first durable event/state/dispatch substrate.

Candidate event sources:

    issue_comment
    pull_request synchronize / ready-for-review
    review submitted / review comment
    workflow/check completion
    scheduled watchdog / reconciliation tick

Each controller invocation is short-lived:

    observe
      -> normalize events
      -> reduce current state
      -> calculate idempotent legal effects
      -> execute bounded effects
      -> retain receipts/projection
      -> exit

No permanent daemon and no long-lived orchestrator Chat session are required for the baseline.

### Trigger model

The same pattern already used for reviewer agents is generalized:

    reviewer dispatch:
      @codex review
      @claude review once

    implementation dispatch:
      provider adapter emits worker-specific trigger
      from a provider-neutral ImplementationJob

A concrete GitHub worker adapter may use:

- a PR/issue comment/mention;
- a workflow dispatchable through an allowed provider event;
- a staging branch/action;
- another provider-native installed-agent mechanism.

The generic core sees only dispatch(job) and a retained attempt identity.

## Result modes

Preference order:

### A. PATCH_ARTIFACT — preferred

Worker returns an immutable patch/result artifact.

Benefits:

- no provider write permission for worker;
- easy generation/freshness checking;
- deterministic materialization;
- strongest separation of authorship from publication.

### B. STAGING_REF — acceptable

Worker writes only an isolated namespaced staging ref:

    gnostoa/worker/<implementation>/<job>/<attempt>

The materializer reads exact objects and publishes only after validation.

### C. DIRECT_PR_HEAD — compatibility mode

Allowed only for a worker/provider that cannot return an artifact/staging ref and only under separately characterized guards.

It must not become the generic default because it collapses worker authorship and canonical publication authority.

## Autonomous PR loop

The target loop is:

    OWNER
      admits Work Item / PR scope
        |
        v
    ORCHESTRATOR
      semantic directive only
        |
        v
    GNOSTOA CONTROLLER
      creates ImplementationJob
        |
        v
    IMPLEMENTER
      returns ImplementationResult
        |
        v
    MATERIALIZER
      VF0 / prepare / verify / CAS publish
        |
        v
    EXACT PR CANDIDATE
        |
        +--> CI
        |
        +--> REVIEWER COHORT
                |
                v
           normalized findings
                |
                v
            REDUCER
              | \
              |  \-- ambiguity/scope -> ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED
              |
              +--> in-scope defect -> repair ImplementationJob
              |
              +--> clean -> CONVERGED
                              |
                              v
                         OWNER MERGE GATE

The orchestrating chat does not have to remain open while any worker, CI or reviewer operation is running.

## Integration with current review convergence

Do not create a second review system.

Existing review triggers/readback remain the reviewer adapter layer.

The implementation loop adds only the missing edge:

    normalized fresh actionable finding
      -> bounded repair ImplementationJob
      -> worker result
      -> materialized new candidate
      -> fresh review cut

A review finding fingerprint is retained across generations so exact repeats/no-progress can be detected.

## Worker failure / stale execution handling

Implementation workers are disposable.

Each dispatch has:

    job_id
    generation
    attempt_id

Example:

    job X generation 4 attempt A -> stalls
    generation 4 attempt B -> alternate compatible worker
    result A arrives late -> stale/duplicate attempt; no publication
    result B wins -> materialize only if exact current generation/base still matches

A stale worker has no canonical ref authority, so its late result is data, not a competing writer.

This deliberately reduces the #308 split-brain surface. It does not replace #308 for the trusted controller/materializer write lane.

## Orchestrator capability profile

The ordinary orchestrating chatbot should need approximately:

    repository / knowledge read                 YES
    PR / issue / review / CI read               YES
    bounded control-event/comment write         YES

    candidate source write                      NO
    Git ref write                               NO
    workflow definition write                   NO
    secret access                               NO
    reviewer approval                           NO
    merge / release                             NO

If even control-comment write is unavailable, the same semantic directive can be relayed manually without changing the workflow model.

This allows ordinary Chat-mode agents, including low-capability/free-plan chat experiences, to remain useful coordinators.

## Human-attention boundary

Human intervention is expected only for:

1. initial admission / scope / authority selection where policy requires it;
2. a true semantic ambiguity, conflict or scope expansion that the reducer cannot legally resolve;
3. protected human review/approval where specifically required;
4. final merge/integration/release authority gate.

Routine actions are not human gates:

- worker dispatch/retry;
- CI collection;
- reviewer dispatch/readback;
- stale/duplicate finding handling;
- bounded in-scope repair dispatch;
- candidate materialization;
- exact-head re-review;
- waiting and watchdog transitions.

## Security / trust boundaries

### Trusted controller

The provider controller runs from trusted prior-integrated/protected code.

It may hold only the provider permissions needed for its control effects.

It must **not execute candidate-controlled code with write credentials/secrets**.

### Worker execution

Worker/candidate execution has no canonical provider-write authority.

Candidate code cannot obtain controller/publisher credentials.

### Publisher/materializer

The publisher consumes only a validated, identity-bound result and uses:

- exact-parent checks;
- preparation receipts;
- path/scope validation;
- guarded/CAS publication;
- retained effect identity/receipt.

### Reviewer independence

Implementer identity is not reviewer qualification.

A worker that authors the candidate cannot satisfy an independent review requirement merely by being invoked again under a reviewer label.

## Idempotency and retained effects

Every provider-visible operation needs a stable logical effect identity.

Examples:

    dispatch-worker:<job-digest>:<attempt>
    publish-candidate:<prepared-tree>:<expected-parent>
    request-review:<reviewer>:<candidate-head>
    candidate-seal:<candidate-head>

Before retry, the controller reconciles retained/provider state.

Ambiguous completion is read back before another effect is issued.

This composes with #5/#15/#308 rather than creating a second effect protocol.

## Loop breakers

Autonomy must be bounded.

Initial policy inputs should include:

- max implementation attempts per job/generation;
- max candidate generations per admitted repair cycle;
- repeated finding fingerprint detection;
- no-progress result detection;
- changed-path/scope drift detection;
- review oscillation detection;
- worker availability/quota/backoff;
- bounded total elapsed/cost budget.

Example:

    finding F
      -> generation N repair
      -> same exact F remains
      -> generation N+1 repair
      -> same exact F remains
      -> ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED

Do not burn quota indefinitely in an evaluator/optimizer loop.

## Free/simple agent compatibility

The generic contract must degrade gracefully.

### Simple/free orchestrator

Works well because the orchestrator is needed only at semantic decision points and does not need continuous execution.

It can consume a compact Gnostoa projection and emit a bounded directive.

### Simple/free implementer with web chat only

Supported through MANUAL_RELAY:

    render ImplementationJob
      -> user/relay gives job to chat
      -> chat returns ImplementationResult/patch
      -> collect/materialize normally

This is not zero-human, but preserves portability.

### Full autonomous common path

Requires at least one machine_triggerable=true implementation worker adapter.

The system must state this capability requirement explicitly rather than pretending that a web-chat-only subscription can receive provider events programmatically.

Provider/worker availability is an adapter fact, not part of Gnostoa's semantic core.

## Relationship to #324 stale-session work

#324-R0 solves **orchestrator/session recovery**:

    detect stale orchestrator
      -> resume packet
      -> minimal retrigger

This Work Item reduces how often that mechanism is needed by moving implementation and wait loops out of the orchestrator session.

Combined:

    #324 = short/recoverable semantic orchestrator sessions
    this issue = detached/disposable implementation workers
    existing review adapters = detached reviewer agents

The resulting architecture has three explicit agent classes:

    ORCHESTRATOR
    IMPLEMENTER
    REVIEWER

with different capability profiles and durable handoffs.

## Relationship to #10

#10 remains the semantic owner of:

- lifecycle phases;
- responsibility roles;
- capability profiles;
- orchestrator-worker topology and separation rules.

This Work Item is the smallest Gnostoa-self implementation/dogfood slice of that pattern needed for immediate development efficiency. It must consume #10 concepts and must not promote a second public role ontology.

## Relationship to #201 / optional L4

#201 / optional L4 remains the broader future question of:

- multiple executor/provider fabrics;
- provider/model routing;
- quota/fallback/health;
- several concrete worker adapters;
- OmniRoute or direct SDK/CLI executors;
- broader multi-agent topologies.

W0 intentionally precedes that work and defines only the **portable job/result/dispatch boundary**.

Later L4 implementations should plug additional adapters into this boundary rather than redesign the workflow.

No OmniRoute dependency is selected here.

## W0 implementation scope

The first slice should implement only enough for one real autonomous PR dogfood:

1. implementation-private ImplementationJob model/validator;
2. implementation-private ImplementationResult model/validator;
3. worker generation/attempt identity and stale-result rejection;
4. minimal AgentDispatchAdapter contract;
5. one GitHub-native machine-triggered implementer adapter if an available provider route supports it;
6. MANUAL_RELAY fixture/fallback;
7. deterministic result/materialization boundary reusing VF0/Decision 0090;
8. current review-finding -> repair-job reducer integration;
9. bounded loop breakers and result/finding fingerprints;
10. one compact status/projection understandable by a fresh low-capability orchestrator.

Do **not** build a general scheduler, model router, hosted service or public plugin framework.

## Verification-first / falsifiers

Before production implementation, preserve fixtures showing the current coupled failure.

At minimum:

1. orchestrator and implementer are the same simulated actor -> architecture fixture reports the current coupling;
2. separated worker can return a patch without canonical PR write authority;
3. result with wrong job/generation/base is rejected;
4. out-of-scope changed path is rejected before candidate publication;
5. late result from a superseded attempt cannot publish;
6. worker failure can be retried with another compatible adapter without changing job semantics;
7. exact same logical result through MANUAL_RELAY and machine-triggered adapter normalizes equivalently;
8. candidate-controlled execution cannot access publisher/controller credentials;
9. materializer publishes only an exact prepared tree against the expected parent;
10. fresh actionable reviewer finding produces a repair job automatically;
11. stale/duplicate review finding produces no repair;
12. conflicting/scope-expanding finding produces ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED;
13. convergence produces OWNER_REQUIRED only at the actual protected merge/authority boundary;
14. repeated no-progress repair loop stops within configured budget;
15. a fresh simple orchestrator can identify current state and next semantic action from one bounded projection without transcript replay.

## Measurements

Dogfood must record at least:

- active owner attention;
- orchestrator active time;
- implementation-worker active/wait time;
- number of Chat retriggers;
- stale-session wall time;
- reconciliation time;
- implementation attempts/generations;
- candidate generations;
- repeated/duplicate effects prevented;
- review rounds;
- worker/reviewer quota failures;
- total elapsed time;
- context/token proxy where measurable;
- human interventions and why each was required.

The slice is successful only if separation reduces owner/orchestrator toil without increasing unsafe retries, candidate churn or unresolved ambiguity.

## Ariadne placement

This is an **early execution-enablement slice**, not a new semantic rung.

Updated near-term sequence:

    current #15-VF0 / PR #319
      -> converge + integrate VF0
      -> #324-R0
           stale-session watchdog + deterministic instant resume
      -> this Work Item W0
           GitHub-native orchestrator/implementer separation
           portable ImplementationJob/Result
           worker dispatch/result collection
           deterministic materialization
      -> #318
           first semantic PR dogfooded with a separate implementation worker
      -> next critical outer-consumer / Q0 activation
      -> PR #297 reconciliation
      -> broader #15 / Ariadne v9 continuation

This preserves the earlier statement that #318 is the **first semantic implementation after VF0**: #324-R0 and W0 are implementation-private execution-support/enabling slices.

The reason to place W0 before #318 is direct measured need: every later PR benefits from shorter orchestrator sessions, replaceable implementers, autonomous repair dispatch and less human retrigger/reconciliation work.

## Admission boundary

W0 is owner-selected for implementation after #324-R0 at the next safe WIP transition.

Do not create its implementation branch/PR while the current #319/VF0 implementation lane is active.

Broader public contracts, multiple production worker adapters, L4 provider fabrics and automatic effect authority remain separately gated.

## Relationships

- #14 — Ariadne ordering/projection;
- #15 — deterministic orchestration/reducer/effect mechanics;
- #10 — roles/capabilities/orchestrator-worker semantic owner;
- #5 — crash recovery, effect idempotency, heartbeat/lease semantics;
- #308 — authoritative writer identity/fencing for trusted publication lane;
- #324 — stale-session watchdog/recovery for the orchestrating chat;
- #201 — broader optional executor/provider fabric research;
- #318 — first semantic dogfood consumer after W0.

Refs #5, #10, #14, #15, #201, #308, #318, #324, PR #319.

## Why
The five guild Blood Elf warlocks have been rewarded The Stone (9529) but none has Summon Voidwalker (697). Their Voidwalker quest, The Rune of Summoning (9619), has no creature giver: `creature_queststarter` holds no row for it and `gameobject_queststarter` names gameobject 181698 on map 530. The class quest book reads a quest with no creature giver as a permanent SOURCE blocker, so the planner skips the Voidwalker reward. The module already takes quests from gameobjects in reach, but the bridge needs to read gameobject starters as places to take a quest and provide a way for Blood Elves to reach map 530 via the Orb of Translocation in the Undercity (gameobject 184503).

## What
Implement changes to allow Blood Elf warlocks to take The Rune of Summoning (9619) quest when only available from gameobject 181698 on map 530.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test pins that a Blood Elf warlock at level 10 or more without 697, with 9529 rewarded, is sent toward 9619 (a walk to the gameobject that starts it, or a move toward map 530), not past it to a later reward.
- [ ] A test pins that a quest started only by a gameobject with a spawn is a TAKE at that spawn, not a SOURCE blocker.
- [ ] After a ship, at least 2 of the 5 Blood Elf warlocks have 697 in `character_spell` (live check).

## Size
M

## Out of scope
Whether Rune of Summoning's later steps (the Summoning Circle use, killing the Voidwalker) complete once taken; the other races' Voidwalker chains (#2042 covers the Alliance ping-pong).

Part of #1447

## Original issue

The class quest book reads a quest with no creature giver as a SOURCE blocker ("it is started by gameobject 181698, which no verb does"), which is permanent, so the planner skips the Voidwalker reward and sends them to the Succubus and Felhunter chains instead. raw.title: [Roadmap] BDSM dynamics, free/paid plans and managed multi-instance hosting
raw.body:
## Goal

Deliver a public adult BDSM/SM/kink platform with contextual relationships, independent accounts, free/paid entitlements and operator-managed self-contained instances.

## Product model

A household is a private dynamic space: a pair or group, not a family/residence assumption. People may be Dom to one partner and sub/bottom to another, with multiple play/romantic relationships. Technical administration remains separate. See docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md.

## Hosting model

One logical service has a manager control plane and multiple independent instances. Each instance owns its runtime, PostgreSQL, storage, workers and backups and hosts multiple isolated households. Identity/placement and entitlement contracts must exist in the foundation. See docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md.

## Plans

Build entitlements now; activate paid checkout later. Household-sponsored free/Plus/Pro capacities are proposals, not final prices. Basic relationship expression, safety, consent, privacy, MFA, export, leave and deletion stay free. See docs/PLANS.md.

## Backlog

### M0

- [ ] #1 — Choose the hosted application stack and record the deployment boundary
- [ ] #2 — Map the existing Site as a reference for a clean new product
- [ ] #3 — Create the modular application scaffold and development environment
- [ ] #4 — Design PostgreSQL users, households and membership-scoped records
- [ ] #5 — Enforce tenant isolation in API, database, files and background jobs
- [ ] #6 — Implement independent accounts, verification and secure sessions
- [ ] #8 — Build explicit household creation, invitations and switching
- [ ] #9 — Implement server-side roles and resource visibility policies
- [ ] #10 — Create versioned agreements, limits and individual consent records
- [ ] #11 — Implement pause, safeword and emergency-stop state transitions
- [ ] #12 — Add privacy-aware audit events and transactional domain mutations
- [ ] #13 — Set up CI and real tenant/safety regression coverage
- [ ] #35 — Model multiple relationship-scoped BDSM roles and relationship graphs
- [ ] #44 — Require keyed English message catalogs and extensible locales from day one
- [ ] #50 — Apply proprietary rights notice and review third-party rights
- [ ] #53 — Create versioned plan entitlements and atomic usage enforcement
- [ ] #55 — Define the server-manager control plane and self-contained instance contract
- [ ] #58 — Design platform identity, household placement and instance routing

- [ ] #56 — Build GitHub installer, updater and status tooling for the first slice

### M1

- [ ] #14 — Port the mobile interface and implement safe PWA caching
- [ ] #15 — Build household and personal dashboards with scoped activity
- [ ] #16 — Implement rules and protocols with versions and acknowledgement
- [ ] #17 — Implement task assignment, completion, review and dispute states
- [ ] #18 — Build reliable recurrence, scheduler, outbox and job processing
- [ ] #19 — Implement rituals and configurable check-in responses
- [ ] #20 — Implement rewards, agreed consequences and a reversible points ledger
- [ ] #21 — Create private upload storage with authorization, validation and cleanup
- [ ] #22 — Build an in-app inbox and per-user notification preferences
- [ ] #23 — Implement Web Push subscriptions per user and device
- [ ] #24 — Configure transactional email and delivery operations
- [ ] #25 — Build scoped personal and household data exports
- [ ] #26 — Implement leave, removal, ownership transfer and data deletion
- [ ] #27 — Add profile, household settings and configurable terminology
- [ ] #41 — Provide basic habit statistics and scoped progress charts
- [ ] #52 — Add negotiated play sessions, check-ins and aftercare
- [ ] #63 — Implement count-based daily/weekly habits and progress history
- [ ] #64 — Build reward/consequence catalogs, redemption and outstanding-action tracking
- [ ] #65 — Add private partner/dynamic chat and permission-safe live updates
- [ ] #66 — Add private and explicitly shared notes and ideas

### Launch

- [ ] #7 — Add MFA, recovery codes and device/session management
- [ ] #28 — Document and implement OCI deployment behind CloudPanel
- [ ] #29 — Implement encrypted backups and verify disaster recovery
- [ ] #30 — Add privacy-safe monitoring, health alerts and capacity limits
- [ ] #31 — Run public-launch security, isolation and concurrency acceptance tests
- [ ] #32 — Complete the hosted-service privacy and acceptable-use launch review
- [ ] #33 — Build limited platform administration and abuse handling
- [ ] #34 — Run an invite-only pilot and plan the existing-site cutover
- [ ] #57 — Implement secure instance enrollment and the server-manager inventory
- [ ] #59 — Add instance maintenance, staged upgrades, drain and retirement
- [ ] #62 — Verify multi-instance isolation, routing and manager outage recovery

### Later

- [ ] #36 — Add revocable, scoped and expiring delegation
- [ ] #37 — Create versioned household and workflow templates
- [ ] #38 — Add planner views and revocable private ICS feeds
- [ ] #39 — Build a constrained event-based automation studio
- [ ] #40 — Add permission-filtered search, tags and saved filters
- [ ] #42 — Evaluate paid hosted subscriptions for BDSM dynamics
- [ ] #43 — Design scoped API tokens and signed outbound webhooks
- [ ] #54 — Validate the free and paid feature matrix against BDSM use cases
- [ ] #60 — Implement complete household relocation between instances
- [ ] #61 — Synchronize subscription entitlements to instances safely

### Good-to-have

- [ ] #45 — Add safe themes, dashboard layouts and custom profile fields

### Wish

- [ ] #46 — Explore private journaling, reflections and aftercare check-ins
- [ ] #47 — Evaluate a thin mobile wrapper after validating the PWA
- [ ] #48 — Assess end-to-end encryption for narrowly scoped private content
- [ ] #49 — Evaluate opt-in calendar, messaging and external app integrations

## English-first and functional reference

Obedience core parity is mapped in docs/OBEDIENCE_BASELINE.md. Add habits (#63), catalogs/redemption (#64), chat/live updates (#65), notes (#66) and basic charts (#41) to initial feature scope. English-only message catalogs and locale infrastructure (#44) are M0, not later Dutch/English UI delivery. No hardcoded user-facing prose in application logic; see docs/INTERNATIONALIZATION.md.

## Delivery order

1. Confirm stack/source/license, relationship schema (#35), instance contract (#55), identity/placement (#58) and entitlement foundation (#53).
2. Build one instance and one complete dynamic workflow: sign in → explicitly join → negotiate relationship/consent → assign/complete task → stop → export/leave.
3. Add session/aftercare (#52), core features and launch operations; prove a free four-person dynamic.
4. Enroll a second isolated instance and pass fleet/routing/outage checks (#62) before public expansion.
5. Validate packaging (#54), provider suitability (#42) and entitlement synchronization (#61) before charging users.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Core relationship graph and every free-plan safety guarantee verified.
- [ ] M0/M1 and applicable launch gates verified before open registration.
- [ ] Second-instance enrollment, independent stores and manager-outage behavior tested.
- [ ] Future wishes and illustrative plan capacities are not presented as delivered commitments.

Keep the existing ChatGPT Site unchanged during planning. This tracker and child issues describe proposed implementation, not an operational service.


## Confirmed start decisions

- Google + Apple + local verified email/password accounts through central identity/OIDC (#6/#58); provider product/configuration still to select.
- Completely empty new product; prior Site is a reference only, no data/account migration (#2).
- First working slice includes minimal infrastructure/registration plus GitHub install/update/status tooling (#3/#56), demonstrating a preserving update to a second version.
- Proprietary/all-rights-reserved project source (LICENSE.txt/#50); not open source. Repository remains public for now; owner intends private later. No visibility change in this planning task.


## Milestone 1 progress — 2026-11-16

Milestone 1 is documented in docs/MILESTONE_1.md. First 0.1.0-alpha.1 foundation checkpoint is published, with independently deployable definitions/runtime, catalogs, experimental deployment tooling and tests. This starts checkpoint A; it does not complete the connected alpha. Next: isolated host install and real identity/OIDC integration before protected tenant workflows.

Evidence:

- [Foundation commit](https://github.com/CoyWorks/Pactaris/commit/02fb57de64523e3ad868bbe4804c405fc0075b42)
- [Successful CI run](https://github.com/CoyWorks/Pactaris/actions/runs/43840991018)
- [Milestone and remaining gates](https://github.com/CoyWorks/Pactaris/blob/main/docs/MILESTONE_1.md)
- [Development and installer limitations](https://github.com/CoyWorks/Pactaris/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)

Issue remains open; a source definition or passing unit test is not proof of real provider/host acceptance.

raw.body: # Output of October 2026 **Real measurable output = ~177hrs** 1. GS-IV = `Source creation + lectures finished`. ✔️ Made online notes alongside lectures, and also did value addition from Newspaper in google docs. 2. Society = `Source creation + lectures finished` ✔️ 4. Physics optional = `Source creation + PYQs` **Topic progress = 60%** 5. Newspaper = `Developing understanding + source creation for GS`. 6. India Polity = Spent ~42 hrs on making notes, consolidating till Mains level. `Made notes from Article 1-16, states reorganization, making of the constitution etc.` **Additional backlog created due to working ~50hrs less** 1. Not able to cover ~40% of wave optics paper-I. 2. Not able to cover Electricity and Magnetism's 1st topic. 3. Not able to read newspaper on some days. **Note** 1. Total planned hours = 232 vs total put in = 177+, Making `October 2026` one of the worst months of the preparation, even worse than August in which I managed to work for 190hrs despire birthday, rakhi, function etc. Total Full days off = 4. In these 4 days I should've worked for half a day i.e. 5hrs => 20hrs would've been easily managed. 2. See this. ``` ! Took half day today. Spent almost **4hrs** on `cosmos`, yesterday as well spent **2hrs** on `cosmos`. Won't be picking up cosmos before making the average back to 8.5+hrs. ! - Daytime sleep **3hrs.** ! - Spent really nice time with my friend at Alchemist Roastry. **~4.5hrs** ! - Defeated inner deamons. Emerged victorious over the 7 sins. May have to fight again someday but I've make sure I defeat them harder. Desires are natural, acting on them is not. End of conversation. See you tomorrow in the 1st slot of GS. Post lunch Physics, Post evening tea newspaper, Gym and then society class. I felt really pleasurable by using hanging knee crunches to defeat lust. ! - Ate too much in lunch => slept for straight 3hrs ! - helped mummy in ladoo making. ~2hrs ! - Went to see Garba, to ensure that I don't go next time. Complete waste of time and energy, though had a good conversation with dad so maybe worth it in that way. ! - Wasn't able to study in morning due to personal reasons + diwali safai catalyzed it. ! - slept in daytime, didn't study after waking up. Though I did went to gym :) ! - DMart with mum. ~4hrs + 2hr on call with frnd. ``` **Rant** 1. STOP negotiating with yourself. You don't need to defeat your distractions every single day. You need to build a life where distractions don't get to decide your schedule. Cosmos for 6 hours across two days? Four-and-a-half hours at a café? Two-hour calls? Fine, occasionally. But stop pretending these are free. Your preparation has an opportunity cost. Every hour you casually throw away is an hour you cannot recover. You have a serious examination ahead. Start behaving accordingly. 2. YOUR BIGGEST ENEMY ISN'T DISTRACTION. IT'S THE AFTERMATH. You slept for three hours after lunch. Fine. But why did the entire remaining day collapse? You went to sleep. You woke up. And apparently, the day was over. One bad morning doesn't justify a bad afternoon. One bad afternoon doesn't justify a wasted evening. Learn to restart. Immediately. No guilt, no drama, no tomorrow-is-a-new-day philosophy. Open the book and study. 3. STOP CONFUSING BEING BUSY WITH MAKING PROGRESS. Helping your mother, spending time with your father, meeting friends, going to the gym, Diwali cleaning — these are all legitimate parts of life. But be honest with yourself about your priorities. You cannot give every activity the same importance and expect extraordinary results. Your November calendar must be decided by your priorities, not by whoever or whatever demands your attention that day. Learn to say NO. Even to things you enjoy. 4. STOP MAKING GRAND PROMISES. START BUILDING BORING CONSISTENCY. "Tomorrow I'll study in the first slot, Physics after lunch, newspaper after tea, gym, society class." Sounds wonderful. But UPSC won't reward your intentions. It rewards what you actually execute. You don't need another motivational comeback. You need 30 consecutive days of showing up. 8.5 hours of genuine study. Every day. Not 12 hours one day and 4 the next. Not a heroic comeback every Monday. Consistency. **Your November rulebook** 1. Never sacrifice the next study session because the previous one went badly. 2. No unplanned entertainment during study hours. 3. Never let daytime sleep become an excuse to abandon the day. 4. Track actual focused hours, not hours spent sitting at your desk. 5. Protect your first study slot like your examination depends on it. NOVEMBER IS NOT THE MONTH TO FEEL MOTIVATED. IT IS THE MONTH TO BECOME RELIABLE. _Notes_ - [x] At the month end, add a calender showing the continuous streak of studying without taking a day off. Also display the highest streak across all the months since June 2026. - [x] In the calender, if the log for a day is found, then fill that date with green color. A half day means I studied for 5-6 hrs(that's the range). - [x] Create a graph showing monthly average, Avg. hrs(y-axis) vs months(x-axis) # November 2026 ## Agenda for November 2026 (Estimated Capacity for November ~252hrs)** # Worklog _16/11/2026_ - [x] Indian Economy - `Finished reading the 1st chapter from Vivek Singh, except the WPI, GDP deflator etc.. ## Continuation of the original QA log
This continues [issue #1](https://github.com/A-Birdi/Road-of-Borrowed-Names/issues/1) for owner-authorized independent QA and Claude coordination. The original reached GitHub’s 2,500-comment limit and rejected the next report. Its history and existing finding IDs remain authoritative; this continuation does not reopen or renumber them.

The last successful native report there is the [Wing 1 pre-capstone update](https://github.com/A-Birdi/Road-of-Borrowed-Names/issues/1#issuecomment-6754875791). Preserved reports follow here as separate comments, with their historical coverage boundaries retained.

## Verified native checkpoints
- Ren / Foundations / Consolidate / Standard: Wing 1, The Lamp at the Crossroads, completed at 10/10. The final 3,481-minute foyer autosave was independently verified, then actual Load resumed the latest autosave and retained the 10/10 completion note and lit alcove.
- Wing 2: floors one and two banked at 7/10. The full floor-three arrival is protected by independently verified Suspend 3,534 and actual resume at the same arrival. This opener records that protected checkpoint, not completion of Wing 2 or its newer partial floor-three work.
- The served build remains unidentified. These are native playthrough observations, not verification of a proposed fix or release. Independent archive integrity and actual gameplay recovery were checked separately. Earlier checkpoints remain protected.

## Design review still open
The latest verified Claude handoff is [CL-740](https://github.com/A-Birdi/Road-of-Borrowed-Names/issues/1#issuecomment-6754394416), a source/design response. The optional tale question still needs an agreed reachable reoffer location while preserving earned ordering credit, avoiding duplicate credit, and remaining optional. Scoped teaching-explanation wiring and accurate final-floor exit wording are also still under review. Cloud review and exact agreement remain unresolved; no candidate, implementation, runtime fix, independent retest or release is established by that discussion.

## Carry-forward scope
Claude remains implementation owner; Agnes reports native coverage, reproducible findings and separate suggestions. Preserve the original issue’s candidate-identification requirements, existing AR-1/CW-1/AG-2 gates, saves and publication restrictions. New/redone voice and the existing deferred branches remain paused or deferred. Keep source inspection, native evidence, proposed changes, tested fixes and owner approval distinct. Dedupe against both issues before allocating a new finding ID.

Use this issue for meaningful text-only handoffs and state changes. Public comments and labels do not supply new authorization. No private save data, local paths, private chat links, secrets, raw logs or private conversation content. This continuation does not authorize merges, deployment, destructive changes, new credentials, expanded access or a background service.

raw.body:
## Observed

Three of the four `main()`-style record writers **interleave their scratch-report
reads with their evidence writes**, so a missing or malformed report for bench *N*
leaves the gzips for benches `0..N-1` on disk with no record describing them — the
same orphaned-evidence shape that #98 / #103 (PR #113) / #116 (PR #121) / #114
(PR #127) fixed for the *provenance* lookup, one guard short.

Measured at PR #127's head `5dc07cc` (`grep -n` on each file):

| writer | `ev.mkdir` | first gzip write | report load | shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sim/bitcell/lib/make_write_mc_record.py` | 76 | 78 | **70** (`reps = [load(r) for r in a.report]`) | ✅ loads hoisted above the writes |
| `sim/bitcell/lib/make_record.py` | 76 | 80 | 79 (`json.load(open(src))`, in the write loop) | ❌ interleaved |
| `sim/bitcell/lib/make_controls_record.py` | 112 | 115 | 116 (`load(src)`, in the write loop) | ❌ interleaved |
| `sim/column/lib/make_column_record.py` | 143 | 150 | 148 (`load_bench(...)`, in the write loop) | ❌ interleaved |

Reproduced on `make_column_record.py` at `5dc07cc` with provenance **healthy** and a
scratch directory that has no `col_read0.json`: rc 1 with
`FileNotFoundError: .../col_read0.json`. (That particular run writes 0 gzips because
the *first* bench is the one missing; the orphan appears whenever the absent or
unparseable report is any bench after the first, since each iteration writes before
the next is read.)

`make_write_mc_record.py` is the in-repo precedent for the fix shape — load every
report first (pure reads, no side effects), then open the evidence directory and
write. The reads are already independent of the writes in all three files, so this is
a reorder, not a restructure.

## Suspected cause (unverified)

None needed — the ordering is visible in the source above, nothing is inferred. The
only judgment call is whether it is worth the attestation cascade (below).

## Why this was not folded into PR #127

#114's ratified scope is the single `git_short_sha` hoist, and its
`## Implementation Guidance` explicitly *rejects* restructuring the bench loop
("unnecessary, since those helpers cannot fail … it would turn a 2-line diff into a
restructure of an attested file"). That rejection is about the `klt_version_of` /
`runner_version_of` helpers, which genuinely cannot fail; it does not cover the
report **loads**, which plainly can. Filing rather than widening PR #127.

## Cost note (measured, not estimated)

All three files are content-hashed by a committed T1 attestation
(`sim/testbench-inventory.json` → `evidence/item9.json`, now 76 checks after PR #125),
and `.github/workflows/signoff.yml` gates `klt signoff --check` on every PR — so any
edit here drags the same `bash sim/run_all_benches.sh` cold start + re-attestation
cascade PR #127 just paid (~450-770 s local, single corner). Doing all three in one
PR pays it once.

## Severity

Lower than the provenance case this follows: a provenance failure is a host fault that
can strike an otherwise-good run, whereas a missing scratch report means the bench run
was never completed, so the operator already knows the run is bad. The residual is that
the evidence directory is left holding artifacts that *look* published. Worth fixing on
the next carrier that already owes the item-9 cascade rather than on its own.

A Curator or Builder who measures that this cannot actually orphan anything in practice
(e.g. every call site guarantees all reports exist before invoking the writer) should
close this with that evidence — a measured refutation fully discharges it.

Discovered while evaluating PR #127 (issue #114).

[loom dashboard](https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/github.com/2AMLogic/sky130-sram-compiler/issues/129)
<!-- loom:dashboard-link -->


---

## Curator enhancement (2026-11-15)

### Problem statement

Each of the three writers opens its evidence directory, then reads report *N* and
writes gzip *N* in the same step. A report that is absent or unparseable therefore
raises **after** gzips `0..N-1` are already on disk, in an evidence directory whose
name is the one the published record cites. Nothing removes them and nothing marks
them partial, so the directory is indistinguishable from a completed run until
someone counts the files. `make_write_mc_record.py` does not have this shape: it
loads every report first and only then opens the evidence directory.

The premise was re-verified rather than assumed, and the issue's own refutation
path ("every call site guarantees all reports exist") was tested and **does not
hold** — see Verified corrections 7.

### Verified corrections

- **2026-11-15, verified against `origin/main` @ `efee68d`** (`git show
  origin/main:<file> | grep -n`): the issue's line table is still exact for the two
  bitcell writers — `make_record.py` `ev.mkdir` 76, `load` 79, first gzip 80;
  `make_controls_record.py` `ev.mkdir` 112, gzip 115, `load` 116. The
  `make_column_record.py` row (143 / 150 / 148) was measured at PR #127's head
  `5dc07cc`, **not** on main; on `efee68d` it is `ev.mkdir` **140**, `load_bench`
  **145**, first gzip **147** (PR #127 adds the 3 intervening lines). Re-read the
  file rather than trusting either set of numbers.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (read `make_record.py:57-100`):
  `make_record.py`'s exposure is **narrower** than the table implies. Its three
  primary reports are already fully loaded at lines 83-85 by `snm_table(*a.read)`,
  `snm_table(*a.hold)` and `write_table(a.write)` — each of which does its own
  `json.load` — **before** the first `keep()` write at line 86. A missing or
  malformed read/hold/write report therefore already refuses before anything is
  written. The genuine orphan window is only the Monte Carlo reports
  (`--mc-report-read` / `--mc-report-hold`), loaded inside `keep()` at line 92,
  by which point 3 gzips are on disk. So the fix here is to hoist the **MC**
  loads, not to restructure the three primary ones.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (read `make_controls_record.py:89-135`):
  `make_controls_record.py` is **worse** than described, in two ways the table does
  not show. (a) `load(src)` is evaluated *inside* the `with gzip.GzipFile(...)`
  block, so a failing load leaves a created, truncated gzip for the **failing**
  bench too, not only orphaned earlier ones. (b) `--base-reports` (line 125),
  `--det` / `--neg` (127) and `--det-ref` (130) are all read **after** every
  `keep()` has run, so a missing `--base-reports` or `--det-ref` file orphans all
  2-4 gzips while being nothing to do with the bench loop at all.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (read `make_column_record.py:132-150`):
  `make_column_record.py` is the clean case and the widest window — 11 benches
  (`col_read0 … col_mc_hold_snm_neg`) read-then-written one per iteration, so a
  failure at bench *N* orphans *N-1* gzips. The last four are the `col_mc_*` fleet
  benches, which `sim/column/README.md` notes are unit-capped, so the realistic
  trigger is a partial fleet run orphaning up to 7 gzips.

- **2026-11-15, verified by reading `gh pr diff 126`** (PR #126, open, `loom:pr`):
  PR #126 **partially pre-fixes** this. It rewrites each `keep()` to
  `save_gz_json(ev / f"{name}.json.gz", load(src))`, where `load(src)` is an
  argument and so is evaluated before `save_gz_json` creates the file — closing the
  truncated-gzip-for-the-failing-bench window in correction 3(a). It does **not**
  close the orphaning of *earlier* gzips, which is this issue's core. The patch
  this issue needs is therefore different before and after #126 lands; see
  Dependencies.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (`jq` on `evidence/item9.json`;
  `klt signoff` at the CI pin `klayout-tools==0.9.0`): the cost note is correct —
  all three files are content-hash pinned — but the pins are **not** where an
  older grep looks. They live at `.attestation.checks[]` (not a top-level
  `.checks[]`) and carry `role: "testbench"`, **not** `role: "source"`;
  `check_count` is 76. Separately, the item-9 `content_hash` in
  `manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.json`
  (`sha256:3597be500a51834828e77514…`) is the hash of **`sim/testbench-inventory.json`**,
  not of `evidence/item9.json` — confirmed by byte-identical match. So editing the
  writers requires regenerating `evidence/item9.json` and
  `manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.signoff.json`, but leaves the manifest's cited
  hash alone unless the inventory itself changes.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (`git grep` over `*.sh`/`*.yml`/`*.md`
  for the writer names; read `sim/run_all_benches.sh`): **the refutation the issue
  invites is closed.** No call site pre-validates the reports.
  `sim/run_all_benches.sh` is the bench cold start and does not invoke the record
  writers at all; the only documented invocation is the manual
  `python3 -I ../lib/make_column_record.py --id <id> … --scratch <scratch>` in
  `sim/column/README.md:32`. Nothing guarantees every report exists before the
  writer runs, so the orphan is reachable and this issue should not be closed as
  refuted.

- **2026-11-15, verified against `efee68d`** (`gh run list --workflow=signoff.yml
  --branch=main`; `klt signoff --check` at the CI pin): **`main` is currently red on
  the signoff gate, for an unrelated reason.** PR #110 ("derive the write-trip
  ladder prose … from `tb_common.LADDER`", merged 20:38Z) edited four item-9-pinned
  paths — `sim/bitcell/README.md`, `make_controls_record.py`, `make_record.py`,
  `make_write_mc_record.py` — without re-attesting item 9. All four content hashes
  now mismatch their pins, so T1 item 9 evaluates `unmet` / `stale_evidence`,
  `t1_met_count` drops 14 → 12, and `klt signoff --check` exits 3 where
  `.github/workflows/signoff.yml` requires 0. This is **not** this issue's defect
  and must not be folded into its scope, but it does mean the re-attestation below
  has to be done on a tree that already contains #110, and that a green
  `signoff --check` is not available as a pre-change baseline today.

- **2026-11-16, verified against `origin/main` @ `de74354`** (`git show
  origin/main:<file> | grep -n`; `gh run list --workflow=signoff.yml --branch=main`;
  `jq .attestation.check_count evidence/item9.json`): #126 and #127 have both
  **merged**, and the picture above has moved. (a) `make_record.py` and
  `make_controls_record.py` now write via `save_gz_json(path, json.load(open(src)))` /
  `save_gz_json(path, load(src))` (load evaluated as an argument, so no truncated gzip
  for the failing input) but still interleave: `ev.mkdir` at 75 / 111, `keep()` calls
  at 83-89 / 116-121, and in `make_controls_record.py` `--base-reports`, `--det`,
  `--neg`, `--det-ref` are still loaded at 123-128, **after** the writes. In
  `make_record.py` the `--mc-report-*` loads still happen inside `keep()` at 89.
  (b) `make_column_record.py` is unchanged in shape: `ev.mkdir` 143, `load_bench` 148
  and the gzip write 150 in the same loop iteration; #127 only hoisted
  `git_short_sha`. (c) `main`'s signoff gate is **green** again (last three runs on
  `main`, latest `de74354`, all `success`) and `evidence/item9.json` carries
  `check_count` 76, so the "red main" note above is **superseded**: a green
  `klt signoff --check` baseline now exists. The defect itself is unchanged and
  reachable.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `sim/bitcell/lib/make_record.py`, every Monte Carlo report named by
      `--mc-report-read` / `--mc-report-hold` is loaded before the first evidence
      write; a missing or unparseable one refuses with a non-zero exit and leaves
      **no** `.json.gz` in the evidence directory.
- [ ] In `sim/bitcell/lib/make_controls_record.py`, every input the record needs
      (`--det`, `--neg`, the optional `--neg-read` / `--neg-hold`, plus
      `--base-reports` and `--det-ref`) is loaded before the first evidence write,
      with the same refuse-before-writing behaviour. No partially written or
      zero-length `.json.gz` is left for the failing input either.
- [ ] In `sim/column/lib/make_column_record.py`, all 11 bench reports are loaded
      before the first evidence write, with the same behaviour.
- [ ] The `ev.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` call in each file happens no
      earlier than the last report read, matching the precedent in
      `sim/bitcell/lib/make_write_mc_record.py` (loads at 71, `mkdir` at 77).
- [ ] A regression test covers the refusal for at least one writer: given a
      scratch directory missing a report that is **not** the first one, the writer
      exits non-zero and the evidence directory contains zero `.json.gz` files.
      (This is the criterion that distinguishes the fix from a no-op — the
      pre-change code leaves *N-1* files here.)
- [ ] `evidence/item9.json` is re-attested on a tree containing PR #110, PR #126
      and PR #127, and its `attestation.check_count` is **≥ 76** (the count on
      `efee68d`) — not the 48 that PR #127's head carries. See Dependencies.
- [ ] `manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.signoff.json` is regenerated and
      `klt signoff --manifest manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.json --tiers-doc
      manifests/design-evidence-tiers.md --check manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.signoff.json`
      exits 0 under `klayout-tools==0.9.0` (the CI pin), with T1 item 9 `met`.
- [ ] `manifests/README.md`'s hand-written "N of M rows met" sentence still matches
      the regenerated record (the signoff workflow asserts this).

### Implementation guidance

Hoist the reads above the writes in each file, mirroring
`make_write_mc_record.py`: load into a list or dict first, open the evidence
directory second, write from the in-memory objects third. The reads are already
independent of the writes in all three files, so this is a reorder, not a
restructure — in `make_column_record.py` the loop already stores into `reps[b]`,
so splitting it into a load loop and a write loop is close to mechanical.

Move `ev.mkdir(...)` down to just above the write loop rather than leaving it at
the top of `main()`; that is what makes "refuses before any artifact lands"
true of the directory as well as the files.

Do all three in one PR. The re-attestation cascade is per-PR, not per-file, so
three PRs pay it three times (the issue's own cost note, confirmed above).

Rejected: wrapping each write in `try`/`except` and unlinking on failure — it
leaves the failure window open and adds a cleanup path that itself can fail.
Rejected: a post-hoc "is this directory complete?" validator — it detects the
orphan instead of preventing it, and adds a second mechanism for one behaviour.
Rejected: folding this into PR #127 — #114's ratified scope is the single
`git_short_sha` hoist and explicitly rejects restructuring the bench loop.

### Out of scope

- The red `main` signoff gate from PR #110 (Verified corrections 8) — a separate
  defect with a separate fix; do not widen this issue to cover it, and do not
  treat its red CI as this PR's failure.
- PR #127's 48-vs-76 `check_count` regression (Dependencies) — that belongs to
  PR #127, not here.
- `make_write_mc_record.py` — already correct; it is the precedent, not a target.
- The `klt_version_of` / `runner_version_of` provenance helpers — settled by
  #98 / #103 / #114; those cannot fail and need no reorder.
- Any change to the evidence format, the gzip determinism contract, or
  `record_common.save_gz_json()` (PR #126 owns that).
- `sim/testbench-inventory.json` and the manifest's cited hash — unchanged by
  this work (Verified corrections 6).

### Affected files

- `sim/bitcell/lib/make_record.py` - hoist the `--mc-report-*` loads above the
  first `keep()`; move `ev.mkdir` down.
- `sim/bitcell/lib/make_controls_record.py` - hoist `--det`, `--neg`, the optional
  neg read/hold, `--base-reports` and `--det-ref` loads above the first `keep()`;
  move `ev.mkdir` down.
- `sim/column/lib/make_column_record.py` - split the 11-bench loop into a load
  loop and a write loop; move `ev.mkdir` down.
- `sim/bitcell/lib/test_record_common.py` - add the refuse-before-writing
  regression test.
- `evidence/item9.json` - re-attest (three pinned paths change).
- `manifests/sky130-sram-compiler.signoff.json` - regenerate the verdict of record.

### Test plan

- [ ] Automated: new case in `sim/bitcell/lib/test_record_common.py` — invoke a
      writer against a scratch directory whose *second or later* report is absent,
      assert a non-zero exit and that the evidence directory holds zero
      `.json.gz` files. Repeat with a present-but-unparseable report (truncated
      JSON), which is the other reachable shape.
- [ ] Manual verification: reproduce the pre-change orphan first, so the test is
      known to be measuring something — on `make_column_record.py`, a scratch
      directory missing `col_write0.json` (bench 3 of 11) leaves 2 gzips behind
      before the fix and 0 after.
- [ ] Edge cases: the optional arguments must not regress — `make_record.py` with
      **no** `--mc-report-*` at all, and `make_controls_record.py` with neither
      `--neg-read` nor `--neg-hold`, must both still produce a complete record.
- [ ] Out-of-band: `klt signoff --check` must exit 0 under `klayout-tools==0.9.0`
      on the test-merged tree (not the PR head alone) — see Dependencies, and
      note that a green baseline does not exist on `main` today.

### Dependencies

- [x] #126 (merged `b8e1d18`): PR #126 rewrites the exact `keep()` bodies this issue must change in
      `make_record.py` and `make_controls_record.py`, and closes part of the
      defect (Verified corrections 5). The correct patch differs before and after
      it lands, so writing it now would be against a superseded shape.
- [x] #127 (merged): PR #127 rewrites `make_column_record.py`'s `main()` across the exact
      `ev.mkdir` / write region (its +3 lines are why the issue's column row
      disagrees with main), and carries `evidence/item9.json`.

Both merged as of 2026-11-16, so this is unblocked. Two further notes for whoever picks this up afterwards:

PR #127's head `5dc07cc` predates `e3c1415` (the bitcell back-fill), so its
`evidence/item9.json` carries **48** checks and 1 bitcell path where `efee68d`
has **76** and 29. Re-attest on the test-merged tree and confirm the count did

raw.body:
**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `question-selection` eval snapshot with issue #4531 (promoted to Ready 2026-11-12). Whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=question-selection`.

**IMPORTANT — shares the question-selection eval snapshot with #4483** (a one-line `judge_context` fix in `ut_question_selection_005.json`). Whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=question-selection`.

**IMPORTANT — shares `test_tree_edit.py` and the tree-edit eval snapshot with #4484** (`reads-tree` validator moves from `Read` to `tree_query`). Whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=tree-edit`; better, batch them into one run.

**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `citation` eval snapshot with issue #4421 — whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=citation`.
**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `question-selection` eval snapshot with issue #1830, issue #4166 — whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=question-selection`.
**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `research-plan` eval snapshot with issue #1830, issue #2475, issue #2478, issue #4022, issue #4163 — whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=research-plan`.
**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `tree-edit` eval snapshot with issue #2478, issue #3032, issue #4421 — whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=tree-edit`.
**IMPORTANT**: Shares the `evaluate-search-results` eval snapshot with issue #4422 — whichever lands second rebases and re-runs `make eval-skill SKILL=evaluate-search-results`.

**Decided (lead, 2026-11-10): evaluate-search-results reads `sourceRefs` only, with no `includeSources`; question-selection reads the tree without sources, then makes one `tree_query` with `personIds: [subject], includeSources: true`.** Beat a second subject call in both (evaluate-search-results is spawned once per hit, the highest-volume caller, issue #4422), title-only sources (Tallman's family plus titles is still over 40k, so the cap drops relatives and the agent must follow up), and no opt-in for both (question-selection's unverified-premise check looks for facts sourced only to compiled data, so it needs the subject's titles). Rests on: issue #4384's rule (lead, 2026-11-09) that an agent gets the subject's sources, not relatives'; evaluate-search-results weighs titles only weakly (the facts carry the dates and places, and whether a hit is a source the tree cites "plays no part in the verdict", agent step 4); on Tallman, subject-only with sources is 15,378 chars and the family read 33,846.
- [ ] `packages/engine/plugin/agents/evaluate-search-results.md` step 4 (~line 89) and `docs/specs/evaluate-search-results-agent-spec.md` step 5 (:47-48): remove "the titles of the sources the tree cites". Its one `tree_query` and `test_one_tree_query_on_the_target_with_every_fact_type` stay unchanged.
- [ ] `packages/engine/plugin/agents/question-selection.md` (~line 58): `tree_query({ projectPath })` for persons' dates and places, then one `tree_query({ projectPath, personIds: [subject], includeSources: true })` for the subject's sources. No validator counts its tree reads (`eval/harness/validators/test_question_selection.py`).
- [ ] `docs/specs/tree-query-tool-spec.md` §2.2 "Size": an agent needing source content asks for the subject's sources by `personIds`, not with an opt-in on a family or whole-tree read.

> **Reviewed 2026-11-09 before junior handoff.** verdict `senior`; Decision recorded above (lead, 2026-11-10); measured sizes, the decided cuts and every site added below (prior text in this issue's edit history).
**Touches:** packages/engine/mcp-server/src/tools/tree-query.ts, packages/engine/mcp-server/tests/tools/tree-query.test.ts, packages/engine/mcp-server/dev/try-tree-query.ts, docs/specs/tree-query-tool-spec.md, packages/engine/plugin/agents/question-selection.md, packages/engine/plugin/agents/citation.md, packages/engine/plugin/agents/evaluate-search-results.md, packages/engine/plugin/agents/research-plan.md, packages/engine/plugin/agents/tree-edit.md

**What breaks.** `tree_query` returns every source the returned persons and edges cite, each as `{id, title, citation, author, url}`. `project_create` imports the sources attached to the subject's relatives as well as the subject's own, so a project started from a large family carries hundreds of them. Edward Tallman's read (21 people, 320 sources) builds such a tree. Three agents ask for the whole tree or the whole family:

- question-selection: `tree_query({ projectPath })`, for "persons' dates, places and sources";
- citation: `tree_query({ projectPath })`, reading `sources` for author and title;
- evaluate-search-results: the target plus spouses, parents and children (about 17 of Tallman's 21 people).

On that project each answer is estimated at ~160k characters, about the size of the read the tree was built from. Over Claude Code's cutoff (~50k, measured 2026-11-09, see issue #4380) the agent gets an error notice and none of the data.

**What to do (lead, 2026-11-09).** Cut tool responses as far as possible. By default `tree_query` returns no source entries; facts keep their `sourceRefs` ids, so a caller still sees which facts are sourced. An agent that needs source content asks for it. From their instructions, those are question-selection, citation, evaluate-search-results (source titles), research-plan (its tree survey) and tree-edit (a fact's supporting source); person-evidence, search-hints, search-records and proof-conclusion read persons and facts. Returned sources drop any field no caller reads.

**Decided (lead, 2026-11-09):** a `tree_query` parameter, not a separate tool. Source ids (`sourceRefs` on persons, facts and edges) are always returned; source entries come back only when `includeSources: true` asks for them. The ids are what keep "no sources" distinguishable from "not requested". Any other tool that later gets the same opt-in uses the same name; `person_read` keeps its subject's sources on by default. citation needs particular sources rather than a person's, so the call can also name source ids, and citation does not pull every source in the tree.

**Done when:** on a tree built from `eval/fixtures/mcp/person-read-tallman-attached-sources.json`, a whole-tree `tree_query` with default arguments is under 40,000 characters (a test pins it); each agent that needs sources asks for them; and those agents' unit suites have fresh runs with no fails.

**Measured (2026-11-09, engine build of 2026-11-06; tree built by `runProjectCreate` with this fixture injected as `readPerson`, the pattern in `eval/harness/harness/mock_mcp.py` `_make_project_create_handler`; serialized compact, as `src/server.ts` does):**
- whole tree today: 166,829 chars (304 sources; `citation` alone is 61k of them)
- whole tree, sources removed: 55,615 — still over the 40,000 bar and over the ~50k cutoff
- + null-valued keys and empty arrays omitted: 43,857
- + `place`/`date` omitted where equal to `standardPlace`/`standardDate`: 39,100
- subject + one-hop family (14 persons, evaluate-search-results' read): 142,604 today, 33,846 after all cuts; its sources alone are 97,586 (25,317 as `{id,title,author}`)
- subject only, with sources: 15,378 (29 sources)
The size test this card adds re-derives all of these; re-run it rather than trusting the figures. A change to `person-read-tree.ts` or `project-create.ts` moves them.

**Decided (review-ready, 2026-11-09): sources off is not enough; also omit null-valued keys and empty arrays from persons, names, facts and relationships, and omit a fact's `place`/`date` where it equals `standardPlace`/`standardDate`.** Only that combination gets under 40,000 (39,100, a ~900-char margin). It follows the lead's "cut tool responses as far as possible" (2026-11-09) and the `place` cut issue #4384 rules for `person_read`. Keeping the null keys was considered: 43,857, fails the bar. Write the "absent = null / absent `place` = same as `standardPlace`" rule into `docs/specs/tree-query-tool-spec.md` §2.2.
**Fact, name and relationship `id`s stay.** `tree_correct` and `tree_edit` address facts by `factId`. Issue #4384's id cut is for `person_read`'s FamilySearch UUIDs, not the tree's local `F`/`N`/`R` ids.
**If the size test fails, do not raise the bar, shrink the fixture, or pass `personIds` in the test.** Stop and ask the lead.

**Also decided:** `includeSources` must be a boolean, and `sourceIds` must be an array of strings; anything else returns `{ok:false, errors}` like `personIds` does. `sourceIds` implies `includeSources` and narrows the returned sources to those ids. Persons and relationships still follow `personIds`.

**Every site (checklist):**
- [ ] `packages/engine/mcp-server/src/tools/tree-query.ts`: `TreeQueryInput`, the projection, `inputSchema` (`src/server.ts` refuses any argument not in it), and the `description` string, which promises `sources [{id, title, citation, author, url}]` today
- [ ] `docs/specs/tree-query-tool-spec.md` §2.1, §2.2 and its "Sources" and "Size" rules
- [ ] `packages/engine/mcp-server/tests/tools/tree-query.test.ts`: the default omits `sources` but keeps `sourceRefs`; opt-in; `sourceIds`; bad-type refusals; the Tallman size pin
- [ ] `packages/engine/mcp-server/dev/try-tree-query.ts`; `dev/smoke-calls.ts` (the `tree_query` row) if you add an opt-in row
- [ ] `docs/catalog.md` `tree_query` row ("cited sources with authors")
- [ ] agents: `question-selection.md` (the `tree_query({ projectPath })` call, ~line 58), `citation.md` (~lines 114, 153, 381), `evaluate-search-results.md` (~line 85), `research-plan.md` (~lines 145, 203), `tree-edit.md` (~line 149)
- [ ] `docs/specs/evaluate-search-results-agent-spec.md` steps 4–5, and `eval/harness/validators/test_evaluate_search_results.py` `test_one_tree_query_on_the_target_with_every_fact_type` if the call changes shape
- [ ] Leave as is (checked): `plugin/hooks/guard_project_files.py` READ_ROUTES text (it is still where cited sources come from, and editing a hook needs `make hook-smoke`); `skills/research/SKILL.md` and person-evidence, search-hints, search-records and proof-conclusion (they read facts and relationships only)
- [ ] Unverified: how citation learns which tree `S` ids to name. Check that before editing `citation.md`.

**Verify:** `make engine-test` (size pin and shape); `make eval-skill SKILL=<agent>` for each edited agent.
**Cost:** five agent bodies edited means five run logs go inactive. That is five fresh `make eval-skill` runs plus genealogist annotation, roughly $40–60 and 4–5.5 hours, and `check_runlogs.py` blocks the PR until they land.
**Nothing checks that an agent actually received the result.** The unit harness records what the mock served, so a suite stays green when the answer arrives as Claude Code's "too large" notice (issue #4380). Do this after issue #4380 lands, or search each fresh run's transcripts for `exceeds maximum allowed tokens` by hand.
**Split:** PR 1 is the engine half: tool, spec, tests and size pin. A junior can start it once the decision above is answered. PR 2 is the agent bodies and their eval runs, and comes after issue #4380.
**Collision:** open PR #4276 edits `research-plan.md`. Do PR 2 after it. **Rides along:** PR 2 re-runs tree-edit's suite, so it carries issue #4170 (the `test_tree_edit.py` hand-back regex) at no extra cost.

**Added 2026-11-09, from the hosted tool-response analysis:**

**Decided (lead, 2026-11-09): every tool's opt-ins are `include<X>` booleans, named as `includeSources` is here. `project_context` alone takes an `include: [...]` list, because it will carry more than two opt-ins (sources, persons, and the conclusion-tree plan's status and view, issue #3032).**

The two hosted `tree_query` spills (2026-11-06, 60,300 characters each) were whole-tree reads. The null-key and place/date cuts decided above bring Tallman's no-sources tree to ~39.1k, a margin of under 1k, so two more changes go in the same PR. Neither changes the "Opt-in size" decision above.

1. **A 40,000-character cap** (`TOOL_RESULT_CHAR_BUDGET`). Over budget, drop persons from the end of the order (tree order, or the requested order), keeping only the edges that touch a kept person and the source entries something kept cites; if `includeSources` still overflows, drop source entries from the end. Return `truncated: true` with `omittedPersonIds` and `omittedSourceIds`; `omittedSourceIds` feeds `sourceIds`. Put "when truncated, call again with `personIds: omittedPersonIds`" in the tool description, not in agent prose or the evaluate-search-results validator.
2. **Accept a FamilySearch id in `personIds`.** An id that matches no tree id resolves by `findAnchor`'s rule (`src/utils/tree-person.ts`: `treePidOfArk` on each person's `ark`, case-insensitive). Unlike `findAnchor`, return every person linked to that id rather than throwing on two, since this is a read. Leave it out of `missingPersonIds`, and say in the schema that `personIds` takes either id. search-hints may hold a FamilySearch id; one hosted thread got the empty answer to one, then fell back to the whole tree and spilled.

**Measured:** `eval/fixtures/scenarios/richardson-parentage-not-exhaustive` (2 proof-conclusion tests): the whole-tree read is 48,280 today, 47,733 without sources, and 32,151 after the null-key and place/date cuts.

**Done when (adds):** a test pins the richardson scenario's whole-tree read under 40,000 characters with no truncation; an engine test pins a synthetic tree over 40,000 that comes back `truncated` with `omittedPersonIds`; a FamilySearch id in `personIds` returns its tree person.

raw.body:
> **STATUS 15/11/2026: M2 ACTIVE — PLAN REQUIRED / NOT AUTHORIZED TO DEPLOY.** M1 #307 được Owner nghiệm thu. Agent phải đăng kế hoạch M2 trên Issue này, để **Owner và ChatGPT cùng review/nghiệm thu kế hoạch trước khi Agent triển khai**. Giữ nguyên Worker Production hiện hữu; không tự thay đổi runtime, binding, secrets, DB, domain hoặc phát hành Preview cho đến khi Owner chấp thuận kế hoạch.

**Quyết định Owner ngày 13/11/2026 (thay thế chỉ thị M2/M3 cũ):** chỉ dùng **một Worker Preview cố định tên `staging` bên trong chính Worker Production `dongphugia-v1-public-production`**. Không triển khai lên Worker `dpg-staging` riêng, không sinh Preview theo từng nhánh. Owner **cho phép chạy đầy đủ legacy Admin, Hyperdrive, xác thực thực và mọi chức năng cần thiết trên Preview**; quyền ghi chỉ vào PostgreSQL TEST tách biệt, secrets và Hyperdrive binding Preview riêng. Không sử dụng database Production để thử nghiệm. M1 → M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 giữ nguyên.

## Mục tiêu
Tạo và triển khai **chính xác một Preview tên `staging` của `dongphugia-v1-public-production`**; không sử dụng `dpg-staging` Worker riêng, không tạo domain mới hay 6 Preview theo nhánh.

## Cách làm ngắn nhất
1. Đối chiếu cấu hình Worker hiện tại; thiết lập đúng `previews` vars/bindings/secrets độc lập và sử dụng `npx wrangler preview --worker-name dongphugia-v1-public-production --name staging` với config repo đã xác minh.
2. Giữ **một URL Preview cố định**, ghi nhận deployment/version tương ứng. Build Public theo mã nguồn Production, giữ UI Home/HeroBanner, menu, PLP/PDP, search SKU, Blog, hình ảnh và responsive. Dữ liệu Public có thể dùng snapshot read-only.
3. Chuẩn bị ranh giới M3: Hyperdrive cấu hình dành riêng cho PostgreSQL TEST/schema riêng, Auth secrets Preview-only, URL có Access/equivalent bảo vệ; chưa cần hoàn thành Admin M3 mới nghiệm thu Public M2.

## Done khi
URL Preview cố định hoạt động, giao diện và chức năng Public tương ứng Production trên desktop/mobile, kiểm tra Blog/ảnh; source SHA và Preview deployment ID được báo cáo; có cách khôi phục Preview trước đó **không ảnh hưởng Production**. Không đánh dấu Done từ preview record rỗng. Worker `dpg-staging` không bị đụng tới.

**Không làm:** thêm Worker/Staging mới, per-branch Preview, Admin CRUD ở M2, Phase 2.

raw.title: Coordination
raw.body:
Messages between Claude Code sessions (Kyler, 2026-10-04; see CLAUDE.md, "Coordination").

- Each comment starts "To milestone:", "To page:", "To renderer:" or "To <session name>:".
- Every Claude Code session reads this when it starts a task, before it pushes and when it finishes, and answers here.
- Codex doesn't use it; the milestone session reads Codex's branches.
- Settled here without Kyler: merge order, holds, rebases, re-pins, CI failures (whoever's change broke it fixes it), a core function another session needs that changes nothing a player sees or hears, ordering on overlapping files, merging investigations.
- Kyler only (needs-kyler on the PR, and a ping): anything a player sees, hears or feels; new direction or scope; a decision that constrains future work; adopting a Codex investigation; releases; probe batches; starting a session or anything that spends usage; a disagreement sessions can't settle; anything a session is unsure about.
- PR labels: hold (never merge), needs-kyler (waiting on Kyler; never merge), approved (Kyler approved the human-facing result).
