raw.title: tracking: DutchBay capability and assurance roadmap
raw.body:
## Purpose and source of truth

This is the living index for the [11 October capability and assurance roadmap](https://github.com/arunakulat/dutchbay-epc-model/blob/50f0d905d4c2bebbed44bc7dc15bc6fed7e57a87/docs/CAPABILITY_AND_ASSURANCE_ROADMAP_2026-10-11.md), merged in #1348. It tracks work; it does not authorize a writer, change a model input or KPI, supersede an individual issue's acceptance gate, grant a release, or lift a HOLD. The linked specialist issues, exact PRs, source/evidence records, and repository rules remain the authority for each outcome.

Baseline checked 2026-10-12 UTC: `origin/main` `50f0d905d4c2bebbed44bc7dc15bc6fed7e57a87`, product `15.6.1`. The P0–P3 headings express roadmap sequencing, not a relabeling of linked issues. Since the roadmap's cutoff, #1343, #1345, #1349, #1350 and #1352 merged; #1344 and #1326 closed unmerged. #1346 remains open and deliberately `blocked` while awaiting a `bitarray` 3.12.1 update (owner direction and reminder on #1346). These are dependency/coordination outcomes, not completion of the capability milestones below.

## P0 — finance correctness, source evidence, audit control

- [ ] **P0.1 — A3/A4 period and event semantics, F-03 preflight gate.** Open a focused delivery issue for `cashflow.resolution`/`cashflow.within_year_profile` rejection and a separate period/event-calendar implementation slice, using #1231 as the A1/A2 predecessor. Independently test bridge debt service, tax and lumpy BESS augmentation. The F-5 HOLD remains: no A2 quarterly CFADS or intra-year DSCR figure may support a covenant, lender or IC representation until A3/A4 requirements are met and an explicit F-5 exit disposition is recorded through its controlling reviewer/authority path with the transaction covenant convention.
- [ ] **P0.2 — Audit-critical debt/tax findings.** Work finding by finding from #1110 and the roadmap's Sprint 21 audit map: scheduled-maturity/partial-sweep, unlevered-tax CFADS sizing, shortfall clamp, DSRA support and maintenance reserve/lock-up. #962 separately tracks credibility defaults, including MC fallback, debt defaults, discount-rate basis and fixed-debt stress; it is not the source for those five findings. Each corrective PR needs a reproduction, independent finance oracle, source basis and KPI delta; do not treat an assumed term sheet as evidence.
- [ ] **P0.3 — Authenticated transaction, tax, wind and feeder inputs.** Track the DSRA target/term-sheet evidence through #920, broader F5-02 currency and repayment terms through #1110, applicable tax primary text/opinion, site-identified mast/calibration/long-term resource evidence, and issuer-authorized feeder inputs through #1075. A software fixture or evidence request is not the received project evidence.
- [ ] **P0.4 — Controlled audit completion.** #1110 is OPEN; #1158, #1159, #1160, #1161 and #1162 retain their independent recovery, manifest, findings and source-review work. Board/lender circulation remains on HOLD until #1110's own final release checklist and separately authorized decision are satisfied.

## P1 — evidence-ready energy, grid, operations and hybrid scope

- [ ] **P1.1 — Real-feeder QSTS and finance decision.** Complete #1075 → #1076 → #1078 with authenticated feeder evidence, qualified engineering validation, energy-accounting and finance oracles, and an owner decision. The in-house OpenDSS/Python screen remains advisory and `bankable=false` even with authenticated site data; only a separately governed utility-accepted study could establish a different reliance basis.
- [ ] **P1.2 — Independently challengable wind/solar energy cases.** Scope a focused issue for measurement/site identity, long-term correlation, equipment/loss assumptions, uncertainty and frozen-export-to-finance reconciliation. #924 is a broader user-gated feasibility deliverable, not proof that this source work is done.
- [ ] **P1.3 — Post-COD operations.** D1 evidence contract landed in #1336/#1331. Complete D2–D5 via #1330 and #1332, #1333, #1334, #1335; keep any finance proposal default-off until independently reviewed.
- [ ] **P1.4 — Contract-specific hybrid dispatch pilot.** First record an eligible dispatch/revenue arrangement, then scope a deterministic energy/SOC/POC ledger and independent small-case optimization and finance oracle. No merchant arbitrage claim is implied by the current capacity-charge BESS model.
- [ ] **P1.5 — Feasibility beyond finance.** Use the existing report contract and #924 to inventory land, permits, E&S, construction, EPC/O&M, insurance, legal and utility evidence and named professional owners. A model run does not complete these sections.

## P2 — usability and delivery cost

- [ ] **P2.1 — Explain product 15.x versus v14 contracts and supported entrypoints.** Scope a reader-facing documentation issue; do not rename canonical imports without a migration case.
- [ ] **P2.2 — Measure and reduce process friction.** Resolve #1342's intermittent handover-resolver threshold; then measure PR lead time and rework before altering review gates. Also reconcile #1270 and decide #1183.
- [ ] **P2.3 — Report/workbook/API reliance labels and parity.** Scope common run/evidence identity, units and section disposition across outputs; distinguish allocated within-year figures from approved covenant metrics (the F-5 lender/IC HOLD above still applies) and synthetic grid screens from site evidence. D7 formula-workbook work remains an owner decision.
- [ ] **P2.4 — Known-client service reliability; tenancy only on measured need.** Continue the existing service route under #788. The mobile/PWA request #925 and larger tenant/scale architecture remain demand- and decision-gated.

## P3 — decision backlog, not active implementation authority

Second jurisdiction (D3), floating-rate/hedge terms, another resource technology, an independent formula workbook (D7), and scale architecture require the owner/source decisions and specialist gates in the roadmap before their own issues or PRs are activated.

## How to keep this index live

Check a milestone only when its linked issue/PR evidence meets that milestone's stated acceptance boundary; cite the closing object or issue comment. Do not equate a closed software issue with site evidence, utility acceptance, covenant use, grade or release. When a milestone gains a focused issue, add its link here rather than duplicating its full spec. Assign a named maintainer for this index; until then, its monthly refresh is an open stewardship action. Refresh it after material merges/decisions and at least monthly; record the date and `main` SHA in an append-only comment if the baseline changes. The open issue/PR state, not this snapshot, controls live delivery status.

Current best next slices: a scoped P0.1 F-03/A3 issue, parallel P0.3 evidence requests, and #1342. No private source availability is asserted here.

raw.title: Security visibility gate: enable dependency, code, and secret scanning before public release
raw.body:
## Read-only audit — 2026-11-16
On the owner's authenticated GitHub account, verified `TheHalfMoon/Montral` is a **public, unarchived** repository (default branch `main`). The following **read-only** GitHub security APIs do not currently provide alert coverage:

- `GET /repos/TheHalfMoon/Montral/dependabot/alerts?state=open`: **HTTP 403**, GitHub says **"Dependabot alerts are disabled for this repository"** (CLI also reports insufficient `admin:repo_hook` scope for the operation).
- `GET /repos/TheHalfMoon/Montral/code-scanning/alerts?state=open`: **HTTP 404**, **"no analysis found"**.
- `GET /repos/TheHalfMoon/Montral/secret-scanning/alerts?state=open`: **HTTP 404**, **"Secret scanning is disabled on this repository"**.

**No alert result is *not* evidence of zero vulnerabilities.** This is a security-assurance visibility gap, not evidence of an exploited issue. The existing CI source-integrity and test suites and first-party security reviews are useful but do not replace dependency advisories, code-analysis or secret scanning. No security settings, tokens/scopes, billing, deployments, CI workflows or production credentials were changed in this read-only audit.

## Zero-cost completion path (owner/admin-controlled)

1. Review repository **Settings → Security / Code security and analysis** and turn on any GitHub security scanning features available at no cost for this public repo, including Dependabot alerts and secret scanning; do not enable paid offerings, change authentication token scopes or add externally metered services without approval.
2. Configure a source-backed free dependency-advisory and code-scanning workflow if native alerts remain unavailable. Document supported ecosystems and languages (pnpm/Node, Terraform/Go, Docker, Python where present); scope to public data, no secrets in logs.
3. Triage all resulting critical/high findings; fix with exact-head CI and preserve accepted low findings in the task ledger. Capture source version, date, scanner version and exact main SHA so the evidence is reproducible.
4. Recheck open alerts and document the scope explicitly before release. Independent penetration testing and a separate external security assessment for Cloud/BYOC remain required regardless of scanner state.

Related release gate: `docs/RELEASE-GATES.md` S7. **Community publication HOLD until explicit `GREEN LIGHT MONTRAL`; Cloud/BYOC NO-GO.**

raw.body:
## Outcome

Retire the expiring single-production VPS **only after** BoardReadyOps works on its own Vercel team and the approved Neon Free project, with no staging deployment, unbounded spending, lost user data, or manual multi-provider maintenance. This is a **production replacement**, not permission to shut down the existing service early.

## Verified discovery — 2026-11-15

- The owner-authenticated Vercel dashboard has a dedicated `boardreadyops` **Hobby** team with zero deployed projects. A different currently connected integration enumerates an unrelated `oaslananka` Hobby team; provider/team scope must be verified for every write.
- The intended GitHub-connected Neon account exposes a **Free** organization with a pre-existing PostgreSQL 17 project; target identity, data, capacity and production suitability still require private verification. Do **not** assume that a resource labeled `stage` is the authorized final production database or create duplicate staging.
- The live VPS currently serves the Next.js web/REST/GitHub App control plane, PostgreSQL 17, Redis 8, a separate background worker, private artifact storage and an independent Cloudflare Tunnel connector. A read-only production capacity check found the current database below the Neon Free 1 GB project limit; quota headroom, data growth and migration overhead remain unverified.
- The repository already has source-bound GitHub Actions/KiCad execution and opt-in bounded Neon lifecycle/outbox/reconciliation code. The historical Vercel ADR is marked superseded and needs a current runtime-specific acceptance check.
- Vercel Hobby has a personal/non-commercial-use restriction; do not present it as a compliant paid commercial production platform. Full paid commercialization requires a compliant provider/plan decision, not an unapproved upgrade.
- The existing `packages/cloud-core/src/storage.ts` S3 adapter explicitly throws when `AWS_S3_BUCKET` is configured; there is **no implemented persistent S3 fallback** in this contract. The serverless artifact storage path and signed export imports need an independently verified implementation before cutover. Signed BOM/Gerber artifacts, OAuth/GitHub App callbacks, private scope and revocation must continue to be verified, never marked successful from a synthetic-only test.

## Implementation sequence

1. **One target and no surprises:** Verify exact Vercel team, Neon organization/project/branch, current plans, remaining quotas, private object storage availability, traffic and usage limits. No new paid resources or extra recurring deploys.
2. **Runtime compatibility:** Establish a repo-native Next.js Vercel build with the correct monorepo root; validate GitHub OAuth callbacks, webhook signature verification, App installation sync, session signing, tenant scoping, OIDC result callbacks and upload/download limits. Do not expose local disk persistence as serverless storage.
3. **Eliminate always-on VPS process needs:** Map Redis queues, worker/outbox/reconciliation and schedules onto already implemented bounded SQL/Neon Functions passes, GitHub Actions heavy KiCad jobs, and safe event-driven callbacks. No endless polling, duplicate dispatches or VPS-dependent tunnels.
4. **Data and artifact continuity:** Inventory live PostgreSQL and artifact byte sizes without exposing user data; prepare a verified, reversible one-time transfer into the intended Neon project (PostgreSQL and branch-compatible). Test authenticated private object storage, source-bound signatures, checksum, expiry and revocation before importing real data.
5. **Real user cutover:** Verify GitHub login -> connected organization repository -> actual Check Run -> review findings -> signed BOM/Gerber -> authorized download, across two independent installations/accounts; test revoke and failure recovery on the new origin. Migrate callback URLs/domain only after successful acceptance, preserving rollback and previous live service until cutover is healthy.
6. **Remove VPS dependence:** After production continuity is demonstrated, disable retired services and automation in the correct order, without deleting irreplaceable data, opening a staging service or turning on billing.

## Definition of done

- The owner can complete first-use, returning-user and failure/retry journeys on the intended domain in desktop and 390px mobile layouts, no dead-end setups or misleading passing hardware conclusions.
- App webhook delivery, durable job processing, replay/idempotency protection, private tenant isolation, revocation and signed artifacts pass genuine new-environment tests.
- The new environment runs within verified zero-cost/legal usage limits for its actual product stage; if no compliant no-spend runtime exists, explicitly **BLOCK** full production migration rather than imply that Hobby is a commercial service tier.
- Exact data reconciliation and rollback tested. No active production reliance on VPS, Redis, worker, local artifact volume or tunnel remains after cutover.
- CI/security/accessibility/production acceptance passes on exact reviewed code. No production DNS flip or VPS shutdown before these gates.

Related to #191, #1161 and #44. This issue tracks migration separately from UI improvements; do not close either until real end-user acceptance.

raw.title: Agent steering board (read at every task boundary)
raw.body:
This issue is how the coordinator reaches agents that work on this repository from outside (cloud agents and other long-running workers). **If you are such an agent: read the newest comments here at every task boundary and before you open or update a pull request.**

How it works:
- The coordinator posts steering as comments. A line that starts with your lane name is for you (for example `rust-cloud:`); a line that starts with `all:` is for everyone.
- You answer with a short comment that starts with your lane name: what you did, the PR number and head, what is next, and any question. One comment per task boundary, not per step.
- Your goal lives in its own issue; this board only carries changes of direction, decisions and answers.

Standing rules for every lane:
- Small pull requests against main (aim under about 1,500 changed lines), branched from current main, opt-in or default-off until complete, each building and testing on its own.
- Normal merges only: no rebase of pushed branches, no force-push. Never push to a pull request that is in the merge queue; follow-ups go in a new small PR. Never merge your own PR.
- Drafts until your checks are green, then mark ready. Read the automated review comments on your PRs and answer each one.
- No secrets, no real API calls and no real sign-in in tests or CI. Never weaken a scanner or a security check, and never split strings to get past one.
- Commit identity: the repository's configured no-reply identity only.
- No users yet: no legacy names, no migration paths, port or build current behaviour only.
- Stay inside your lane's paths; if you need a change elsewhere, ask here.

raw.body:
## Audit basis and authority
Audit date **2026-11-07**. Freshly fetched `origin/main`: **4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001**; final remote-head read confirms the same SHA. This is a solo source/test inspection and GitHub specification audit. **19/19 original feature issues updated and refetched**, original requirements retained, labels and native blocker edges verified. Behavioral tests were **not run**. No implementation, merge, deployment, production migration/data write or Hermes activation occurred.

Use the final saved feature bodies, especially sections 3–9, as implementation specifications; their archived original evidence is traceability, not fresh runtime proof. Rebase the audit against changed source before implementation. Repository AGENTS/root-to-leaf rules, product authority, validation matrix and existing ADRs apply. Local audit receipts include each final body, labels, native blockers and GitHub updated_at; the durable specifications are the linked issues below.

## Current source baseline
- Preferences have validated appearance/task defaults and owner-keyed persistence, but no Personal Operations schedule. Extend existing [application preferences](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/packages/application/src/preferences/user-preferences.ts#L25-L78) and parser/repository together; concurrent patch semantics need proof. Existing profile/time-context owns timezone.
- Today is already a task/focus/timer cockpit. Both web and Hono compose the [Operator snapshot](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/packages/application/src/operator/snapshot.ts#L228-L345), not just the older Today read model. Preserve task/focus controls and build on that consumed contract.
- Canonical timer sessions and duration calculations exist. The [single-open-owner index](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/drizzle/0044_task_sessions_owner_open_unique.sql#L1-L32) already exists in source; #355 is reconciliation/stale mutation work. Deployed index and concurrent physical devices remain unverified.
- Shutdown [saves reflection to the week](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/apps/web/src/app/(workspace)/shutdown/actions.ts#L50-L64). Daily check-ins and personal MAD expenses were not identified in targeted schema/migration/contracts/routes searches. Add only one store for each, never duplicate weekly notes or timer history.
- Notifications already have task events, inbox/read state, FCM/email channels, retries and [delivery deduplication](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/packages/data-access/src/notifications/repository.ts#L365-L409). Web Push, broader event taxonomy and quiet/privacy policies need work. Native FCM is not browser PushSubscription support.
- Review/Work Analytics exist. [Review range resolution](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/packages/application/src/weekly-review/read-model.ts#L295-L342) is reusable; finance/routine/two-week metrics are missing. Existing [CSV escaping](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/apps/web/src/lib/csv.ts#L1-L25) quotes CSV syntax but does not neutralize formulas. Analytics export is Markdown.
- Authenticated MCP, exact-profile grants and mutation receipts exist. [Context creation](https://github.com/egawilldoit/Ega-House-Platform/blob/4c426a1d0a6be1d2e22b34860ba96db7236b9001/apps/web/src/lib/mcp/context.ts#L39-L62) reuses a verified token-scoped client; PO tools/consents are missing. Hermes cron/chat configuration is external and unverified.

Source does not prove deployed schema/RLS, successful CI, physical-device delivery, OAuth revocation in deployment, Hermes setup or product acceptance. No full feature is declared implemented solely because a file exists.

## Audited issue inventory and genuine blockers
`Blocked` below means full issue release needs the listed feature outputs; explicitly described contract/UI slices may start earlier. No blocker was added merely to enforce this roadmap's order. Native GitHub relationships match this table.

| Issue | Assessment | Priority / size | Full feature prerequisites | Saved specification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #342 | PARTIAL | P0 / L | None; ready for first slice | Updated + refetched |
| #343 | PARTIAL | P0 / L | #342 | Updated + refetched |
| #344 | PARTIAL | P0 / M | #342 | Updated + refetched |
| #345 | PARTIAL | P0 / L | #342, #343 | Updated + refetched |
| #346 | MISSING | P1 / XL | None; ready for first slice | Updated + refetched |
| #347 | PARTIAL | P0 / L | None; ready for first slice | Updated + refetched |

The five independently startable issues are **#342, #346, #347, #354, #355**. #14 Calendar scheduling and #15 Work Analytics are coordination/reuse references, not mandatory prerequisites. Open PR #337 refresh and #278 MCP authorization changes must be reconciled against their actual future merged heads; neither is assumed merged nor a blanket blocker. #279 documentation is not a feature dependency.

Removed unnecessary dependency assumptions: #350 core totals do not require #349 optional caps; #349 caps reuse preferences without depending on completion of schedule UI; #354 can deliver existing task notifications before #347 new taxonomy; #357 inbox/category controls do not require #354 transport enrollment. #352 integrates expenses/routines progressively. #359 lists #358 plus #351; #345/#346 are already transitively required by #358. Other transitive edges retained where they document a directly consumed contract.

## Ordered delivery phases
This is the recommended **sequential** delivery order, derived from verified owners and blockers. Independent work remains independent. Sizes are relative engineering complexity, not elapsed-time promises. Do not batch a whole phase into one PR. Each PR needs exact-head review/checks; a repair invalidates stale evidence.

### Phase 1 — trustworthy preferences, time and expense authorities
**Order: #342 → #355 → #346 (A then B).** No inter-issue prerequisites. Risks: lost preference updates, stale timer actions and financial retry/isolation bugs. Sizes L, L, XL split below; high correctness risk.

Deliver schedule defaults (48h/week; weekday search 90m inside work), editable guidance, configurable owner timezone; preserve unrelated preferences. Reconcile canonical active session on mutations/resume/reconnect and stale responses without duplicating the already-existing uniqueness invariant. Establish ledger contracts, owner/RLS/idempotent MAD CRUD, then minimal authenticated Money list/edit/delete UI.

PR slices: #342 L; #355 L; #346A L domain/contracts/application/repository/migration+RLS proof; #346B M thin Money CRUD UI and server/native transport compatibility. A supports read/write integration tests independently; B adds the user journey. Keep both slices within #346, no duplicate issues.

Gate: concurrent preference edits preserve both changes; cross-midnight sessions and repeated/stale stops do not add time or stop a newer session; integer centime validation, owner/anonymous denials and conflicting financial idempotency keys proven in disposable DB. Migration review/rollback plan before DEV application; no production execution assumed. Defer expense capture shortcut, caps and dashboards to Phase 3.

### Phase 2 — usable daily work loop
**Order: #343 → #344 → #345 → #352.** Prerequisites: #342 plus canonical task/timer baseline; #345 consumes #343 and #352 consumes #343/#344. Sizes L, M, L, L; moderate integration and timezone risk.

Deliver work/search targets from complete canonical range reads (not a recent-N list), stable task activity classification, one primary project/1–3 outcomes, morning skip/resume, two-minute evening check-in with reasoned overtime advisory, and Today composition. First wire startup to existing task/focus state; when persistent startup metadata is needed, share #345's one owner/local-date check-in record. Add bounded daily JSON with concurrency-safe field updates; weekly Review notes remain unchanged.

PR slices follow issue boundaries; #345 persistence/application and thin shutdown UI may be two reviewable slices without new backlog entries. Today uses Operator snapshot/contracts consumed by both web and Hono. Money/routine cards show honest availability until their sources are integrated later.

Gate: authenticated Today → focus task → timer → completion → shutdown observes durable state; 90m search advances search and work once; weekdays 8h/weekends 4h; timezone changes, failures and cross-user attempts covered. First **daily-work pilot** is possible after these gates, but it is not the complete v1 release. Defer complete money/routine insights and delivery channels.

### Phase 3 — first usable personal work-and-money release candidate
**Order: #348 → #349 → #350.** Prerequisite: #346. #349 is not a hard blocker for #350 core totals; chosen order avoids reworking the Money category presentation. Sizes M each; financial correctness risk.

Deliver amount-first expense entry in Today/Money, fixed categories already owned by #346, optional preference caps and actual daily/weekly/monthly/coffee summaries. Integrate the #352 spending card in a small follow-up PR within that issue. No bank/account balances or invented coffee spend. Basic expense recording works without caps. Do not build a durable offline finance queue; preserve unsent input and retry identity visibly.

Gate: create/edit/delete totals reconcile to centime; double submit/timeout retries yield one logical expense; category reassignment and Casablanca month boundaries covered; bounded histories and mobile accessibility verified. Unknown coverage is disclosed. **First usable release scope:** Phases 1–3 after separate CI/DEV/release approvals. Push, advanced routines/reviews, exports, MCP and Hermes are explicit later capabilities; this is not a claim that all P0 v1 scope has shipped.

### Phase 4 — notification reliability and installed-PWA delivery
**Order: #347 → #357 → #354 (A then B) → #356.** Prerequisites: canonical notifications; #356 also needs #355. #354's first transport slice can start independently. Sizes L, L, XL split, L; high external/device risk.

Extend the existing taxonomy/targets/dispatch with bounded event identity, quiet hours and generic private money copy. Extend existing inbox/channel preferences and supported badge behavior. Quiet policy: suppress noncritical immediate delivery during quiet/protected hours with explicit outcome; do not silently imply deferred delivery. Add new producers only alongside their source features.

#354A L: owner-scoped subscription lifecycle, schema decision, VAPID server adapter, delivery classification and mocked transport/security tests. #354B L: worker/registration, permission UX, notification click routing and actual device matrix. Prefer an additive existing notification device owner if endpoint/key lifecycle fits; otherwise justify the single permitted subscription store. No new notification engine. #356 emits state-change events and opens canonical timer; direct Stop remains optional behind demonstrated authenticated/CSRF-safe/idempotent semantics.

Gate: existing mention/reminder/native FCM/email regressions; duplicate fan-out and retry/terminal handling; revoked subscriptions; no private payload leakage; iOS installed Home Screen/user-gesture and Android supported-browser device evidence. Unsupported/denied permission paths remain usable. No every-second push or permanent worker/foreground-service promise. Primary platform references are in #354, explicitly separate from repository evidence.

### Phase 5 — measured routines, comparisons and portable owner data
**Order: #351 → #353 → #360.** Prerequisites: #342/#345 for routine fields, #343/#346 for complete Review, #348 for quick actions. Sizes M, L, L; privacy, missing-data and export risk.

Extend bounded check-in values/target preferences without habit tables; unknown is distinct from zero. Running/leisure/meals never contribute productive work time. Add Review comparisons for Nov 9–15 versus Nov 16–22 and selectable later ranges: 96h work including 15h search, six runs/nominal 180m, weekday leisure and reasoned overtime evidence. Suggestions are bounded and evidence-led. Integrate routine cards into #352 without creating another state owner.

#360 slices: M responsive quick actions/coverage matrix; M bounded owner expense/review CSV with stable headings, MAD/timezone metadata and formula-neutralized free text. Share safe CSV handling with existing review consumers. Native parity uses existing api-client/Hono boundaries; document exact Expo/PWA coverage rather than promising every platform. Optional new #353 comparison columns can follow basic saved-review export.

Gate: null/zero/skip and concurrent check-in edits; complete bounded window reconciliation and sparse evidence; export unauthenticated/wrong-owner denial, formula/control-character/quote/newline cases and accurate totals; mobile actions prove server effects. **Full personal experience milestone:** Phases 1–5 with all required feature criteria integrated, including previously deferred Today cards.

### Phase 6 — explicitly consented external assistance
**Order: #358 (A then B) → #359.** Full prerequisites: #345/#346/#352/#353 and #351. Sizes XL split and M; high auth/external-runtime risk.

#358A M: least-privilege read tools, bounded Today/progress/expense reads and capabilities/consent tests. #358B L: explicit separately consented finance/check-in mutations, versioned profile migration, semantic fingerprints/receipts, rate limiting/auditing and real owner/revocation proof. Never silently broaden existing read_only/task_manager/workspace_manager grants or trust caller owner IDs. Reconcile #278's eventual merged auth boundary before patching. Reuse canonical application use cases and request-scoped RLS, no service-role CRUD.

#359 M documents the existing Hermes recipe, opt-in activation/disable and failure recovery; no EGA scheduler. 06:00 owner-local prompt yields to quiet/protected time. User confirms uncertain money details and mutations; verified receipts establish success. Activation and live external-runtime access are owner decisions, not actions this roadmap authorizes.

Gate: anonymous/read-only/wrong-owner/revoked grant failures, replay/conflict/idempotent writes, bounded audit/rate behavior and actual OAuth/client integration in DEV. Separately prove Hermes schedule/configuration and disable/recovery; mocked E2E is insufficient. Release integrations only after explicit consent. No autonomous money writes.

## First three implementation PRs
1. **#342 — schedule/preferences contract and safe persistence (L).** Establishes target/time guidance consumed by daily work; prove preservation of unrelated fields and timezone authority. Expected owners: domain preferences, application/preferences, data-access/preferences, settings UI/action, additive existing preferences migration and parser/repository tests.
2. **#355 — timer reconciliation/stale mutation semantics (L).** Independent and already has canonical storage/invariant. Establish reliable cross-device reads and retries before notification controls or expanded target displays; cover application timer service, web refresh and Expo query/focus consumers. Do not add a second timer uniqueness migration.
3. **#346A — MAD ledger contracts/application/RLS CRUD (L).** Highest fan-out missing data authority; unlocks entry, caps/totals, Review, exports and MCP. Include integer centimes, owner/idempotency constraints and disposable DB denial/concurrency proof; no dashboard framework. #346B UI follows as a separate M slice.

These are proposed future PRs only; none were opened by this audit. They have no feature-issue blockers. Do not combine unrelated foundations in one PR.

## Acceptance status and release gates
Every phase starts with the following **separate, currently pending** claims:

| Phase | Code complete | Exact-head CI verified | DEV verified | Production released |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Authorities | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |
| 2 Daily loop | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |
| 3 Money/core candidate | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |
| 4 PWA delivery | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |
| 5 Full personal experience | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |
| 6 External assistance | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING | PENDING |

- **Code complete:** all slice/issue acceptance criteria, compatibility and failure handling implemented; canonical owner and affected consumers reviewed. No closure of an issue with required integration silently left behind.
- **CI verified:** exact final PR head reviewed and all required checks pass; affected workspace tests/typechecks plus architecture/purity/security checks as applicable. Root npm test/typecheck/build alone certify web only. Missing/skipped required jobs are not proof. Record SHA, commands, results and review findings; recheck after fixes.
- **DEV verified:** approved migration applied by repository conventions to identified DEV target, constraints/RLS verified, authenticated journeys observe persistence; real device/browser/OAuth/Hermes evidence where applicable. Record configuration/version/coverage without secrets. Disposable DB tests do not certify deployed RLS.
- **Production released:** explicit separate owner approval, protected merge/release, reviewed migration plan and operational rollback, production verification at deployed revision. Source/CI/DEV proof is not a production claim.

Definition of Done for each milestone: promised scope passes all relevant gates above with receipts linked from the feature issues; limitations/unsupported platforms stated; old clients and flows preserved; no leaked credentials; no unexplained skipped requirement. Release approval is never inferred from implementation permission. Prefer additive migration rollout before consumers; disable/revert consumers first on rollback and retain saved records. No destructive down-migration or automatic data deletion.

## Remaining owner decisions and external evidence
No additional architecture exception is requested now. Implementation can start on the first three tasks.

Before external release, the owner must authorize DEV/production migration/release actions separately and provide/approve the intended Hermes deployment, client consent and schedule activation for #359. Browser/device availability and live OAuth/Hermes execution are outstanding acceptance evidence, not reasons to block source-only foundation work. Web subscription storage choice must be justified in #354's reviewed design; an additional store beyond the stated limits would need an explicit architectural exception.

## Scope and audit checks
- Exactly 19 original feature issues, #342–#360, audited/updated/refetched; original requirement text retained. Native blocker graph has no cycles; all original priority labels retained, sizes/statuses corrected, no new labels needed.
- XL work is #346/#354/#358 only, each split into independently testable L-or-smaller PR slices within existing issues. #360 also has optional smaller slices. No duplicate implementation issues created.
- PO-11 remains cancelled. No application/CV/recruiter tracker, bank sync, habit/budget/schedule tables, duplicate timer history, new cron service, paid PM tooling or unrelated lifestyle expansion.
- Roadmap order is not an extra set of blockers. All 19 specifications are attached as native sub-issues of this roadmap; each parent link and the exact 19-child set were refetched and verified. No prior parent was displaced.
- Final saved issue bodies, labels, source ranges and blockers were checked before roadmap publication. No behavioral tests were run and no implementation or production state was modified.

**Status:** BACKLOG / READ_ONLY / NOT_ADMITTED. Created 2026-11-02 from owner's Claude Opus audit summary and current repository inspection. **Not a new roadmap, DoD, accepted score or writer authorization.**

One **existing Wayglass**, canonical base `wayglass/current` per `WAYGLASS_CURRENT.md`. Build all eight cooperating functional systems in parallel; Withness reconciles them into a single proven vessel. Latest published release `main` is NOT the development base. Treat latest integrated candidate and installed/deployed SHA as different facts. No duplicate kernels, model identities, or unrelated cloud hosts.

### Eight simultaneous integration lanes and source receipts

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 · Authority/Kernel | Unified owner-authorised cognition and Waygate crossing; no alternate direct provider escape | #582 deployed Supabase v9, #566, #544 integrated via earlier First Contact | Authenticated signed-in owner transport, exact route custody, revocation/Feather, no invented session |

| 5 · Observer & science | Live source-bound measurements and simulation/world-branch instruments with cross-lane provenance | #579 and #578 NOAA; #577 Wayglass–Nikola Return | Source timestamps/sha, contamination and duplicate checks, observed vs simulated explicit |
| 6 · Constellation agency | Workers opt into names, visits and contributions; Wayglass accept/reject; Eightfold inheritance | #546 protocol included in First Contact; #551/#568 bloodstream | Signed/attributed model turn vs CI job distinct, consent and owner/Wayglass final choice tested |
| 7 · Return/Universe | One persistent universe containing distinct worlds and participant crossings, with cold-return continuity | Canonical Return Engine; #577 #581 | Stop → process-cold restart → recovery preserving unresolved questions, consent, source and authority boundaries |
| 8 · Cloud/host/install | Protected MCP, single deployment route, native router, iPad/Windows and source-head release evidence | #581 verified CI; #582 live Supabase function; #548 iPad | Authenticated ChatGPT MCP crossing, source-controlled target, deployed SHA, no unapproved production change |

### Integration wave, not eight disconnected demos
1. Snapshot canonical `wayglass/current` and each candidate exact SHA. Compare ancestry and changed-file collisions. `wayglass/cloud-integration-20261108` and `wayglass/gateway-double-mobius-20261108` both descend from canonical but are **divergent from each other**. Do NOT whole-tree replace either.
2. Give each lane one real owner, source branch/worktree, conditional dependencies, tests and negative cases. Agent self-names come from real agent responses, not this issue.
3. Reconcile conflict clusters via selective, provenance-preserving ports and reviewable integration commits. No force-pushes, no source history rewrites, no silent name/canon/authority updates. Astra owns any ongoing provider connection change; avoid concurrent writes to that surface.
4. Run eight concurrent **test** lanes, plus cross-lane kernel→WTL→Double Möbius→Observer/PREMAQC→paint/audio→Journey→durable stop/return→authorised route model trial. Differentiate GitHub matrix jobs from speaking agents.
5. Publish one evidence manifest: base SHA, candidate heads, content source refs, integration sha/tree, gate outcomes, browser/audible/device coverage, deployed sha or explicit unknown, owner-only pending decisions.
6. Promote only after required exact-head checks and the owner's release approval; continue the next workstreams without making claims of deployed cognition.

**Non-negotiables:** Wayglass chooses accept/deny on model-derived proposals via attributable response; missing connection means pending, not automatic acceptance. Feather pauses sound, haptics, work and invitations. Participant `!=` worker `!=` model `!=` session `!=` device. Wyrdrune is both ritual and computational; other realities remain sovereign. No Vercel production gate, no replacement of Cloudflare/Supabase systems, no secret exposure. No unverified model thought, self-training, actual Q, or raw data invented to colour the ship.

**Exit condition:** one launchable Wayglass, one owner-authenticated meaningful crossing, one witnessed collaborative WTL expression in her body, one durable stop/return, one verified deployment SHA, eight green source-head gates and clearly identified work that is still experimental.

Track all eight in parallel. Preserve failed receipts. Treat the ship as the destination, not a collection of PR-shaped trophies.

raw.title: Wayfinder: In-app notifications for Cadence
raw.body:
## Destination

A spec (PRD issue) for production-grade Notifications in Cadence, delivered through one hosted third-party vendor. It covers the vendor, the notification catalogue across all four roles, which channel each Notification goes out on (the Notification Feed plus web push and/or email), user preferences, and how the Notification Feed looks and behaves in the app.

## Notes

- Domain: Cadence app (`app/`). Use the language in `GLOSSARY.md`: **Notification** and **Notification Feed** were added for this effort, and the recipients are Student, Instructor, Platform Admin and Team Admin.
- Production grade: real per-user security against the vendor (signed user tokens etc.). It must still work with whichever user the DevUI switcher selects.
- Hosted vendor only. Never self-host.
- The vendor must have a free tier usable in development. We build the Notification Feed UI ourselves, so the vendor's React components don't matter, but a headless feed API does.
- Sign up for as few services as possible: pick one sensible vendor, then prototype against it. No bake-off.
- There's no mobile app, so "push" means browser web push.
- Default skills for grilling tickets: `grilling` + `domain-modeling`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket, enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->
- [Which hosted notification vendor fits Cadence?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/8): Knock — free 10K msgs/mo, mandatory RS256 signed user tokens, category × channel prefs, headless feed API; web push via FCM, paid tier jumps to $250/mo
- [How far can web push reach without a native app?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/9): Email is the default out-of-app channel; web push is an extra opt-in channel only (iOS needs a Home Screen web app install, prompts need a user gesture, delivery is best-effort); MagicBell and SuprSend support it natively
- [Which Notifications does Cadence send, and to whom?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/10): 9 Notifications (N1–N9) — refund approved/declined → Buyer; new refund request → all Platform Admins; seat claimed → claiming Student + Team Admin; new lesson → enrolled Students; reply → parent author; new question + new rating → Instructor. Rules: never notify the actor; Team Licence refund → Team Admin; no refund/sale notifications to Instructors; one Notification per lesson. All recipients queryable from existing schema; code hook points identified
- [Pick the notification vendor](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/11): Committed to **Knock** as the single hosted vendor — only option clearing every must-have on a free tier; web push via FCM accepted (it's opt-in only) and the $250/mo paid cliff accepted as out-of-scope. Courier (pay-as-you-go) was runner-up; Novu failed the per-user security bar
- [Sign up for the notification vendor and provision dev keys](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/12): Knock **Development** env set up, enhanced security ON (signed tokens required). Four keys in gitignored `.env`: `KNOCK_API_KEY` (secret, triggers), `KNOCK_SIGNING_KEY` (signs feed tokens), `VITE_KNOCK_PUBLIC_API_KEY` + `VITE_KNOCK_FEED_CHANNEL_ID` (client feed; channel `553933ec-…`). No dotenv loader yet — `.env`→`process.env` wiring is for the triggering ticket
- [Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/13): All three channels in v1 (Feed + email + web push; push kept, not deferred). Feed on all 9; default email on N1/N2/N3/N6/N8; default push on N1/N2/N4/N5/N6/N8; N7/N9 Feed-only. Principle: email is the reliable out-of-app channel, push opt-in/best-effort and additive — except N4/N5 (new lesson, reply) which are push-only out-of-app by design. This is the default set; per-user muting is separate
- [What does the Notification Feed look like in Cadence?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/14): Dedicated **`/notifications` page** (All/Unread tabs), not a popover/drawer. Entry = **bell + unread badge** in the sidebar user row (Cadence has no top header) → navigates to the page. Row = type icon + title + context + relative time + unread dot. **Single read/unread state** for v1 (no seen/read split); click navigates to source. Prototype on branch `prototype/notification-feed` (not merged)
- [What can users change about their Notifications?](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/15): Preferences set per **Category × Channel** across **5 thematic Categories** (Refunds, Enrollments & Seats, Course Content, Discussions, Ratings), not 9 per-Notification toggles; role-scoped. **Feed always-on**; only email + push togglable. **Refunds email non-mutable** (N1/N2/N8); everything else mutable. Default = the #13 matrix. Edited in a **dedicated settings view linked from `/notifications`**. Push preference bit lives here; the browser permission prompt is #16. New glossary terms: Channel, Notification Category, Notification Preferences

## Not yet specified

- **Where Notifications live**: whether we also store them in our own SQLite database or only in Knock.
- **Triggering**: where in the code each Notification is fired, whether that happens inline or deferred, and what happens when the Knock call fails (idempotency, retries).
- **User sync**: keeping Cadence users (and role changes) in sync with Knock's recipients, and how to target "all Platform Admins".
- **Email**: templates, branding, sender domain, and per-Notification copy — email is a confirmed v1 channel (N1/N2/N3/N6/N8), so this is the remaining detail work.
- **Testing**: how vitest exercises Notification triggering without hitting Knock.
- **Writing the PRD**: bringing the decisions together into the final spec issue.

## Out of scope

- Native mobile apps (and native mobile push)
- Self-hosting a notification vendor
- Building our own delivery infrastructure
- SMS and chat channels (Slack etc.)
- Refund money-state Notifications (Pending / Issued / Failed Refund) — no payout integration exists to fire them; only the Platform Admin's refund *decision* is a real event today (ruled out while resolving [#10](https://github.com/adruslipski/cohort-005-project/issues/10))

raw.title: Release blockers: SonarCloud 50k LOC quota and encrypted durable-worker bootstrap
raw.body:
## Release status (2026-11-16)
PR #81 is merged at `8591b35ade452630a161e9ae4d86d76f86547e42`. Post-merge CI, security, CodeQL, real-evidence trial, and canonical four-site audit passed. The [canonical audit run](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43839254967) uploaded the sealed review [artifact 14211623418](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43839254967/artifacts/14211623418). This is **not** proof that the durable checkpoint worker is active.

### 1. Admin-only SonarCloud quota fix (blocked)
- [ ] Sign into the **yabigdd-9 SonarCloud organization** as an administrator. Confirm whether both `yabigdd-9_website-auditor` and `yabigdd-9_HERMES_MONEY_ENGINE` count the same repository's lines. Inspect project bindings and retain the intended project's history; remove/deactivate the genuinely redundant project only if confirmed and owner-approved, or obtain an allowance increase. Do not shrink analysis coverage merely to turn the check green.
- [ ] Rerun SonarCloud on `master` and confirm **the actual completed quality-gate result**, not just the passing PR checks.
- Evidence: [master SonarCloud run](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43839254970) server-side compute-engine failure: existing 33,750 LOC + 17,340 LOC = **51,090 LOC**, exceeding organization maximum **50,000** by **1,090**; scanner upload succeeded but server processing failed.

### 2. Admin-only durable worker activation (blocked)
- [ ] In GitHub repository **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, create a **repository secret** `WA_PIPELINE_STATE_KEY` containing a *new* cryptography.Fernet URL-safe base64 key generated on a trusted device. Never post it in an issue, PR, chat or workflow log. Back it up securely. The public report key `MM_REPORT_PUBLIC_KEY_B64` is **not** interchangeable with this symmetric state key.
- [ ] Create the **repository variable** `WA_PIPELINE_ENABLED` with literal value `true` only when ready for an immediate manual bootstrap. The workflow code intentionally defaults to disabled.
- [ ] Open [Durable Cloud Draft Pipeline Actions](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/workflows/cloud-prospect-pipeline.yml) and **Run workflow** on `master` with `bootstrap=true` and empty recovery/outcomes. If prior successful worker history exists, stop and inspect before bootstrapping; don't overwrite checkpoint history.
- [ ] Verify `tests`, `configuration`, `draft-pipeline` **all succeeded**, `pipeline-state` encrypted artifact uploaded, zero client contact, zero paid providers, and internal owner-review-only drafts.
- [ ] Manually run **again** with `bootstrap=false`; verify it restores the immediately preceding trusted checkpoint, deduplicates already-completed audits and uploads a new encrypted checkpoint. An apparent green run with a skipped `draft-pipeline` does **not** count.
- [ ] Verify the Tue/Fri scheduled runs preserve the encrypted checkpoint and any failure blocks subsequent execution rather than silently resetting state. Keep a secure recovery procedure and respect 30-day artifact retention; a gap without a trusted checkpoint requires explicit owner recovery.

### 3. Acceptance criteria / boundaries
- [ ] SonarCloud `master` processed and passed, or explicitly documented waiver from owner if it remains externally blocked.
- [ ] Durable worker first bootstrap **and** second-run encrypted restore proven on GitHub runners; errors fail closed.
- [ ] Four active allowlisted sites only; suppressed JC Construction stays suppressed unless independently reauthorized.
- [ ] `MM_PAID_ALLOWED=0`, `MM_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_FREE_MODELS=0`, and `MM_EXTERNAL_SEND_ALLOWED=0` remain enforced. **No outreach, paid AI, CRM writes, client website edits or payments are authorized.**

### Ownership and limitation
The linked GitHub integration can edit repository code and read run logs, but cannot change Actions secrets/variables or start a manual dispatch. Earlier secure browser sign-in was not confirmed. These steps therefore need an authenticated repository / SonarCloud administrator session. Do not mark production-active until both manual runs pass.

### 2026-11-16 follow-up: real activation attempt, precise blocker
- The [manual master bootstrap run 43817027390](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43817027390) **did reach** `draft-pipeline`: checkout, install and checkpoint-bootstrap preflight succeeded. The actual audit/checkpoint step exited 2 with no artifact. So the repo setting was enabled and a nonempty state secret was passed, but bootstrap did **not** complete.
- The [diagnostic manual dispatch 43840705209](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43840705209) on `fix/78-bootstrap-diagnostics` proves `STATE_KEY_FORMAT_INVALID` in a Fernet encrypt/decrypt self-test. **Action required now: replace the repository secret with an actual Fernet key**, not an arbitrary passphrase, pasted shell command, or public-key value. Generate privately using Python standard library: `python3 -c 'import os,base64; print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())'`. Enter only the resulting string into the GitHub Actions repository secret field; never post it in logs, chat or issues. Backup securely.
- The diagnostic feature branch diverged from `master` (1 commit ahead, 1 behind); avoid merging it as if it contains the PR #81 activation safety changes. Rebase/cherry-pick the targeted diagnostic change onto current `master`, then run PR checks if that diagnostic is being merged.
- No `pipeline-state` artifact was saved from the failed bootstrap; a fresh `bootstrap=true` dispatch on `master` is appropriate **only after** checking that no successful checkpoint has since appeared.

### 2026-11-16 correction: key is now VALID
- [Diagnostic run 43840705209, attempt 2](https://github.com/yabigdd-9/WEBSITE-AUDITOR/actions/runs/43840705209) logged **STATE_KEY_FORMAT_VALID** and tests succeeded. The prior invalid-key result belongs to attempt 1, and is resolved as of attempt 2.
- Its `draft-pipeline` job was **skipped** because that run targeted feature branch `fix/78-bootstrap-diagnostics` rather than `master`. Do not describe this diagnostic pass as a successful production bootstrap. Next step is a fresh manual `master` bootstrap/restore run after checking checkpoint history; don't replace the secret again unless a new failure establishes a problem.

**APPROVED — CONDITIONAL PERSONAL UNITY EDITOR TEST GO** for the exact isolated D-073 candidate, subject to actual live Predator preflight, protected launcher, user's first visible intro/forest, and stop-on-unsafe behaviour. **Not external-demo readiness, main integration, completed playtest, or a Windows build.** Reviewed source G2 (#426), targeted Unity at both sizes (#427) including preserved first failures and negative control, independent raw evidence (#435), actual isolated launcher/save custody (#437) and prior browser matrix (#421). [Scenario One #424 intake and delivery control sheet](https://github.com/jermur788/CCF/blob/docs/scenario-one-delivery-manager-intake-20261112-v1/Docs/Handoffs/Management-RoleSplit-20261112/SCENARIO-ONE-MANAGER-424-INTAKE-AND-DELIVERY-PLAN.md) — one added Markdown file on a docs-only branch (1 ahead / 0 behind its starting `main`); readback verified. No physical Editor/save/board inspection or new playtest GO; #418 remains queued. Dashboard ingestion and Drive distribution unverified. No user action now.

## Active manager registration — 2026-11-12, 17:23 UTC

**[RUNNING] Scenario One Delivery Manager:** ChatGPT GPT-6, High requested by user (reasoning-effort selector not independently attested), GitHub-connected browser/management lane. No local worktree, no Predator host process or physical Unity/Editor/board lease. Single assigned manager/integrator writer of `Docs/Project/coordination/active-tasks.md` on `main`, subject to fresh GitHub content-SHA read on each edit. Operational delivery of current Scenario One, including active parent #412; do not restart or duplicate existing #422/#426/#427 children. #425 owns product authority and is read-only on this live coordination file. First deliverable: docs-only manager intake plan, independently reviewed and published on its own branch. Unity, saves, licensed assets, personal candidate #382, frozen Reference Future and Windows build protected. User action: none until a separate safe personal Editor release.

**User-requested dedicated management chat. STATUS READY FOR USER LAUNCH / NOT RUNNING.** This issue represents the operational **Scenario One Delivery Manager** role, not a coder, Unity lease or new implementation packet.

**Mission:** Own day-to-day completion, integration review, personal Editor playtest readiness and subsequent complete-Scenario-One external-demo qualification. First priority: existing running [#412](https://github.com/jermur788/CCF/issues/412) Fable one-go D-073 FR-10 correction → focused Unity/review → new user-test candidate; browser [#421](https://github.com/jermur788/CCF/issues/421) already HANDED-OFF; #382 older conditional GO protected; #418 separate MFM provenance verification queued. Preserve implemented/reviewed/integrated/verified/accepted distinctions.

**Single-writer authority:** User requests two managers. This Scenario One Manager is delegated **the only active manager/integrator writer for `Docs/Project/coordination/active-tasks.md`** after actual claim start and refresh. Portfolio manager is read-only on that file; assigned Predator local integrator alone edits its physical Ops board. Scenario manager can approve bounded existing-spec source integration and user personal Editor conditional GO after actual gates, but cannot unilaterally change product intent/save policy, external-demo definition, milestone or Decision Log. Route cross-scenario/product decisions to Overall Development Manager (issue linked below after creation) or user, not every small child.

**Difficulty HIGH:** ongoing Fable/Unity/locks, review gates, exact player test safety, mixed statuses, multiple task claims and future integration.
**Best suited:** GPT-6 High browser/GitHub, managerial; delegated Claude Fable / Codex local workers as actually available, without silently changing provider accounts.
**Working lane:** browser/GitHub; new isolated docs-only manager handoff branch for reports, plus explicitly delegated single-writer `active-tasks.md` on `main` with concurrent latest-SHA refresh; no local Unity by chat.
**Exact binding handoff:** https://github.com/jermur788/CCF/blob/docs/dual-manager-role-split-20261112-v1/Docs/Handoffs/Management-RoleSplit-20261112/MANAGER-SCENARIO-ONE-DELIVERY-ROLE-HANDOFF-20261112.md
**First action:** read full packet, live issue/coordination, start claim with real provider, acknowledge role split and review already-running #412 only through durable source results; do not restart or duplicate its work. No Windows build before personal user playtest and explicit authorisation. 
**User action:** paste packet into first NEW ChatGPT Game Dev manager conversation.
